# Reference

<!-- Generated by `naima docs` from the plugin manifests. Do not edit: change the manifest, then run `naima docs --write`. -->

Everything the loaded plugins contribute, generated from their manifests so it cannot drift from the code.
Every contribution below has a qualified id, `<plugin>/<name>`, and goes by its short name while no other loaded plugin's contribution of its kind takes it. A name stored in the data — a type, field, relation, directory, gate or verifier — is never declared twice; a project that loads two plugins declaring one renames one of them in naima.json. No plugin command may take a name the entry point answers.

## Contents

- [core](#core) — items, fields, links and the invariants every project has
- [trackers](#trackers) — bugs, todos, features, tests, and the archive of closed bugs
- [coordination](#coordination) — claims and session notes, one file per session, recombined from every branch; the timeline, derived from the items and git
- [triage](#triage) — priority, impact, effort, confidence; the urgency ranking built from them; parked, wontfix and dropped deferrals; authoritative documents
- [gates](#gates) — named release conditions backed by items
- [epics](#epics) — epics: bodies of work that group items, their status and progress derived from them
- [discussions](#discussions) — discussions: questions that need time with a person, gathered on the agenda of meetings
- [planning](#planning) — requirements proven by tests, specifications versioned name-vN, the owner's decisions recorded once, and the artifacts the project makes and keeps
- [knowledge](#knowledge) — knowledge entries: facts, hypotheses, findings and lessons, each with its basis — a source, evidence, or other entries — and its kind
- [roles](#roles) — the roles of the company of agents as data: what each owns and refuses, and the kinds of work on its queue
- [announce](#announce) — announceability, computed: a feature may be announced only once user-facing, shipped, documented and checked by a person or end to end
- [loop](#loop) — the non-stop loop: work on an explicit target until only the owner's work is left, then hand him the ordered list
- [beta-markers](#beta-markers) — markers in the code for behaviour shipped without proof
- [verifier](#verifier) — properties checked by formal-methods tools, with each run attached as evidence
- [tools](#tools) — the tools plugins need, installed by Naima into its own directory on the machine it runs on: naima tools reports them, installs one with consent, removes one
- [backup](#backup) — a remote for every repository Naima relies on: the owner is asked once whether to create a private GitHub repository for one that has none
- [verifier-mcrl2](#verifier-mcrl2) — the mCRL2 adapter: a property is a modal mu-calculus formula over an mCRL2 specification
- [ui](#ui) — the views plugins contribute, a provisional window onto the project, shown in a native window or the browser from a server on this machine only, until the new UI replaces it
- [metrics](#metrics) — named measurements — a command's number, a code-quality number taken in process, a test suite's results — recorded per commit, held to a budget, a floor or a baseline, and read back along the commit timeline
- [rules](#rules) — the project's own rules, kept as items: shown to agents first by naima guide, listed by naima rules
- [long-work](#long-work) — long work, run and waited on by Naima: naima run starts a command detached, with budgets and a progress channel, locally or on a host; naima wait blocks on it by its record; naima run list, status, stop and clean; a long run that is due reported and filed, never started on its own; shipped rules make them mandatory for agents and make long work report its progress
- [working-rules](#working-rules) — the working rules every project ships for its agents: quiet, talking to the owner, fast, the coordinator delegating to workers, asking before what cannot be undone, capturing with judgment, never asking what the rules answer, closing every loop; and for everyone, no new status document and the right tool for the job
- [commit-hooks](#commit-hooks) — companion records required in the commit that makes a change, and the path-scoped pre-commit hook that holds them
- [privacy](#privacy) — the owner's material enters the repository only with their recorded yes, and no secret enters it at all
- [adopt](#adopt) — adopt a board the project already keeps as items, in reviewed phases, without losing a line of it or deleting it
- [docs](#docs) — every feature is documented as part of its implementation, and naima check holds it

## Commands at a glance

Every command: what it does, and the policy or invariant it enforces — or nothing, and what it does instead. Each command's manifest says what it does; `enforces` is optional, and `documented` notes a command without it.

| Command | Plugin | What it does | What it enforces |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`init`](#naima-init) | core | make the git repository around the program a Naima project, as its first run does by itself: beside the program, a git clone of Naima at naima-tracker/naima/, create naima-data/naima.json, locked to the clone's origin and its HEAD, which must be on the origin's main — with the release's version and checksum when the installer unpacked a release into it —, and the tracker folder's README.md and .gitignore; print the line that keeps the program out of each host tool configuration it finds (deno.json, tsconfig.json, .prettierignore); and write what makes an agent run naima hello at the start of every session: the line that tells agents where Naima is and to run it, into the host's AGENTS.md, else the first entry file it has, else a new AGENTS.md, and the hooks of each agent tool the project uses that has them (naima.json's agents; absent it, those whose files the project holds and the one Naima runs inside): a session-start hook that runs naima hello, and a turn-end hook that runs the tick when the agent ends its turn; for a repository that is public on GitHub, offer the topic naima, for the agent to ask the owner before adding it (never for a private one); nothing else outside naima-tracker/ is touched unless --write-excludes is given | the program is locked to a commit of its source's main, with nothing uncommitted; outside the tracker folder, only the pointer line, the session-start hooks and, with --write-excludes, the exclusion lines are written |
| [`update`](#naima-update) | core | move the lock to the newest release of the source, or to the version or commit --to names: download the release's archive, check it against its SHA-256 and against the commit its tag names, and record the version and checksum with the commit (a source that publishes no releases, or --main, follows the head of its main instead; a lock that still names a commit of main moves to the newest release once, and says so; a commit of main past the newest release stays until a newer release; with no network the lock stays where it is, and says why); say what changes (the commits, the change notes they add — breaking first, then those that ask an action —, the data formats, the rules added or removed, the options it no longer reads), fetch it into the program, check it out, rename and remove options in naima.json as the change notes say and remove those it reads nowhere, each said with its value, and record the new commit; moving forward, the new Naima finishes: it migrates the data if its format moved, names the rules agents acknowledge again, runs naima check, and files an item in the type with the trait follow-up for each problem or note that is new since the commit before; writes, and says, what makes agents run naima hello at every session start where it is missing — the pointer line, rewritten when it does not say so, and each session-start hook as naima init installs them; all as one change to commit; the only command, with rollback, that moves the lock; with --mode, set what a session start does about a newer Naima | the lock moves only to a release whose archive matches its checksum and its tag's commit, or, for a source without releases or with --main, to a commit of the source's main, with the data migrated forward in the same change; never back past a migration, which runs forward only; a source naima.json names other than the program's origin is refused, by every command, until --accept-source |
| [`rollback`](#naima-rollback) | core | move the lock back to the one naima.json recorded before it, found in its git history, as one change to commit: what update --to does with that commit, its version and checksum recorded again when it named a release | the lock goes back only to a commit that reads the data's formats: a migration is undone by reverting its commit, never by running an older Naima on newer data |
| [`hello`](#naima-hello) | core | what an agent says first in a session: the banner (I'm Naima, the No-guesswork Artificial Intelligence Meta-Agent, active in this repository, with its version and commit); then, as naima.json's updates says, whether a newer Naima exists and, under update, what it changes and its rehearsal, as update --check says them; then where the project is going, as the plugins say it, such as the nearest gate with a due date and the next release, each with its verdict as naima gates gives it; then, one line each, what waits on the owner's decision, such as a long run that is due, never started, or that nothing does; then what it offers on request: what the plugins offer, such as generating code from a model the project has, then what Naima is and its documentation, an update check, an update after the owner's yes; last, the offer to explain what Naima can do from the basics (docs/guide/the-basics.md). Under --hook, the agent is told to open its first reply with the introduction, its name in bold, and how to explain the basics | it never moves the lock nor starts a run; it asks the source only when updates is check or update, and records that check as the day's, and the session it starts (naima origin), in the tick's state outside the repository; the only thing it may write in the project is an urgent message the tick raises |
| [`tick`](#naima-tick) | core | run the tick now, as every command does before its own work: each job that is due — the update check once a day, unless updates is off; the jobs plugins contribute, such as the due long runs once an hour — run by whichever naima process wins it, a failed one retried an hour later, a week of failed update checks raising an urgent message; then say what is due to the owner, each message once, an urgent one once an hour until the owner acknowledges it (naima messages). Every other command says them after its own output, on standard error, one line each: NAIMA-MESSAGE, a space, and the message as a JSON object with the keys id, level (info, warning or urgent), text and ack, where ack is the command that acknowledges it, or null for a message said once | no lock: every decision is a file created only if it does not exist, kept outside the repository in the clone's git directory, so any number of naima processes, in any worktree of the clone, run each due job once; nothing is applied and no long work starts: it finds and says |
| [`subagent`](#naima-subagent) | core | run as the sub-agent-start hook of that agent tool, named as naima.json's agents names it: put the project's rules for agents, as naima rules --audience agents prints them, in the starting sub-agent's context, in the form the tool's adapter gives, and mark, by the sub-agent's id, that it has them, so the tool's guard lets its calls through; the guard holds the calls of a sub-agent with no mark until it runs naima rules, and the hook on its stop sends one that never had them back to read them (docs/agents/read-the-project-rules.md) | it never fails and never blocks a sub-agent from starting: a project that does not open, or an input with no agent id, prints nothing and leaves the guard to hold the sub-agent until it reads the rules; the mark is kept outside the repository, in the clone's git directory |
| [`plugin`](#naima-plugin) | core | turn a plugin on or off, or set one of its options, in naima.json's plugins table — validated the way the project is validated on every load, instead of a hand-edit of the file | a name must be a first-party plugin (loaded or opt-in) or one the table already names with its own source; an option set on one whose options are known here must be one it declares; the whole file is re-validated before it is written, so nothing a later load would refuse ever reaches disk |
| [`stances`](#naima-stances) | core | list the stances available to adopt — plugins of the kind stance, each a set of authored choices and rules a project takes as a whole — with what each says of itself, marking those this project has adopted; for now they are the repositories named naima-stance-<name> of the naima-project organisation on GitHub, asked of GitHub's public API without credentials; with no network, it says it cannot reach it | nothing: it only reads |
| [`stance`](#naima-stance) | core | adopt a stance, show the ones adopted, or list a stance's examples. adopt <name> resolves the name to its repository, github.com/naima-project/naima-stance-<name>, pins the commit at the head of its default branch in naima.json's plugins as stance-<name> (its module plugin/index.mjs), loads it, and runs its adoption when it declares one: its own command stance-<name> with adopt, given the arguments after the name; adopting again moves the pin to the newest commit. status shows each adopted stance, its pinned commit, and whether a newer one exists. examples <name> lists the example paths an adopted stance declares, each with where it is in its checkout, from the project's root | a stance is pinned by commit, as every plugin from git is, and the whole file is re-validated before it is written; what is adopted must declare the kind stance, or naima.json is put back as it was |
| [`guide`](#naima-guide) | core | inside a project, first print what its plugins contribute to the guide, such as the project's active rules for agents; then where the running Naima's documentation is: the skill, the docs map, the guide for people, the rules, the pages for agents, the format, installing; read them as files | nothing: it only prints |
| [`help`](#naima-help) | core | list every command the loaded plugins provide, with its usage | nothing: it only prints |
| [`new`](#naima-new) | core | open an item | every field is validated against its type's declarations before the item exists, and every write hook runs: a typo or a refusal leaves nothing behind; an archive type takes no new item |
| [`show`](#naima-show) | core | print one item: fields, links in both directions, attachments, prose | nothing: it only reads |
| [`list`](#naima-list) | core | list items, most urgent first | nothing: it only reads |
| [`set`](#naima-set) | core | set fields on an item; an empty value removes the field | every pair is validated against the declared fields and passes every write hook (a status moves only along its type's transitions, and each plugin's own hooks); nothing is written unless all pass |
| [`note`](#naima-note) | core | append a dated, attributed note to an item's Notes section: the writer's own words, never a person's message pasted in; earlier notes are never rewritten | notes are append-only and attributed: the writer is named, earlier notes are never rewritten, and a note holds no heading of its own |
| [`describe`](#naima-describe) | core | replace an item's description, keeping its title line and its Notes section | the title line and the Notes section stay as they are: a description holding a title or a Notes section is refused |
| [`link`](#naima-link) | core | link two items; only this direction is stored, the inverse is derived | the relation is a declared one and an item never links to itself; only one direction is stored |
| [`unlink`](#naima-unlink) | core | remove a stored link; a target that no longer exists is named by its id | only a stored link is removed: an inverse is derived, never stored |
| [`move`](#naima-move) | core | move an item to another type, keeping its id and links; refuses a status or field the new type does not declare | the id and links are kept; a status or field the new type does not declare is refused unless --force |
| [`check`](#naima-check) | core | run every invariant; exit 1 on any problem | every invariant the loaded plugins declare (their checks): exit 1 on any problem; with --staged, the ones the pre-commit hook runs |
| [`waive`](#naima-waive) | core | exempt one check's finding on one subject, a problem or a note, with the reason, as a recorded waiver: `naima check` no longer reports the finding, so a problem no longer fails it, and lists the waiver as a note instead | a waiver names a loaded check, a subject that check reports a finding on now, a reason and who waived it; it is one new file under waivers/, and one waiver per check and subject |
| [`board`](#naima-board) | core | print a type's board, grouped by section, most urgent first; at its foot, the summary sections that stand beside the work, such as the metrics | nothing: it prints derived state, never stored |
| [`view`](#naima-view) | core | print a plugin view — as text, its data as JSON, or markdown; without a name, list them | nothing: it prints derived state, never stored |
| [`summary`](#naima-summary) | core | where the project stands, in one screen: every plugin's section | nothing: it prints derived state, never stored |
| [`plugins`](#naima-plugins) | core | list loaded plugins, the extension points each declares, what each uses of the others, and what each contributes to every point; a contribution's qualified id is <plugin>/<name>, shown when its short name is shared or renamed | nothing: it only reads |
| [`types`](#naima-types) | core | list item types, their statuses and fields, then every field's list of values with how many items hold each | nothing: it only reads |
| [`runs`](#naima-runs) | core | list the external programs the loaded contributions declare they start (a model checker, say), which the launcher allows besides git | nothing: it lists the programs the launcher allows besides git; the launcher refuses any other |
| [`messages`](#naima-messages) | core | list what Naima has to tell the owner: the urgent messages not yet acknowledged, which the tick shows at most once an hour, then what it said once, such as a newer Naima; with ack, the owner acknowledges a message, which stops it being shown, in every worktree and, once the tracker is committed, on every machine | a message is acknowledged only by the owner's command, never on their behalf; an acknowledgement is never undone |
| [`origin`](#naima-origin) | core | say the session this worktree is in; with a session id, list what that session filed (each with who asked) and every other item it changed, to review a session that drifted and undo it item by item; with --backfill, give every item with no origin one inferred from git; with --set, settle who asked for an item, such as one the backfill left unknown | an origin is never changed but for who asked, and only through --set, which keeps the rest as it was and records each correction in the origin: what it was, who set it, when; the backfill writes only to items with none, marks each inferred: true with askedBy unknown, for the owner to settle in a review; the session's log is read from outside the repository and never committed |
| [`close`](#naima-close) | trackers | archive a resolved item: fixed, and proven by an item that has passed; or a finished review or decision, with the reason | an item is archived only when fixed and proven: fixedOn set and a verified-by item that has passed, with every write hook agreeing; --force takes a hook's refusal on, for the one who owns the evidence. --reason closes, without fixedOn, proof or commit, only a todo whose kind is review or decision and whose status is done or dropped; the reason is kept in closedBecause and naima check lists it |
| [`bugs`](#naima-bugs) | trackers | how many bugs have no code written, and how many are fixed but unproven | nothing: it only counts |
| [`open`](#naima-open) | coordination | start a piece of work: a worktree <worktrees>/<what> on a new branch <who>/<what> from the trunk, and its claim on the items, in one step | work happens on its own branch and worktree from the trunk, and its claim on the items is recorded in the same step; a branch that already exists is never reused, and the refusal says whether it is merged into the trunk; no worker worktree is opened beyond the option maxWorkers, and the refusal names the open ones and how to raise the bound |
| [`claim`](#naima-claim) | coordination | record that this branch is working on items (writes one file on this branch) | a claim belongs to a branch, never to a detached HEAD nor to the trunk, and is one file on that branch; it never locks anything: several branches may claim one item |
| [`release`](#naima-release) | coordination | drop this branch's claim on items; the last one removes the file, unless the branch is being prepared (claim --preparing) | only this branch's own claim is dropped, and only on items it holds; while the branch is being prepared, the emptied file is kept |
| [`claims`](#naima-claims) | coordination | who holds what, recombined from every branch, with what each branch's worker is doing now | nothing: it only reads; a claim whose last sign of life (its step, or its branch's last commit) is more than silentAfter minutes old (15 here) is flagged possibly stuck; a stale claim (branch gone or merged into the trunk, or every item closed) is listed apart, at the end, and released by naima prune --write |
| [`land`](#naima-land) | coordination | land a branch on the trunk as one marker commit: a merge whose tree is the branch tip's and whose message names the items it closes (Closes: trailers); the shortcut for git merge --no-ff once the trunk is the branch's ancestor | runs from the main checkout on the trunk, clean in tracked files; refuses a branch the trunk is not an ancestor of, one still holding a claim, one that names no item (unless --tracker-only gives the reason and the branch changes only tracker data, or --meets names a requirement it meets) or an item open and not fixed; refuses --meets for an item that is not a requirement, one with no item that verifies it and passed on the branch tip, one whose proofs all passed on the trunk already, and one an item refutes, and one that changes a behaviour path of a repository with changes/config.json (the project, or a submodule) with no change note added, unless --no-change-note gives the reason; refuses, touching nothing, a branch a landing check finds failing, whatever flag is given, and one that changes what has proofs not current — a property or a test suite reading a file it changed, outside models in development — as the landing checks find them on the branch tip's files, unless --stale-proofs gives the reason; moves the trunk only from the commit it read (compare-and-swap); once landed, adds the marker to the commits of each item it closes whose type has that field, in one commit on the trunk right after the marker, so that naima close finds a commit reachable from the trunk; then prints what every landing report says of the files the landing changed, never undoing it |
| [`guard`](#naima-guard) | coordination | the trunk guard: whether it is on and runs in this clone; off turns it off for the project (recorded in naima.json, the hook removed), on turns it back on; server, on the owner's word, makes a GitHub ruleset that lets only the repository's admins push the trunk (with gh, else it says the request and the web page; --print only says them) | while on, the git hook refuses a commit, merge or fast-forward of the trunk made by hand (naima guard-check says what passes); off is the owner's choice, recorded, and update does not put the hook back |
| [`guard-check`](#naima-guard-check) | coordination | what the trunk guard's git hook runs when the trunk is about to move: exit 0 when it may, else one line saying why not and what to do | a commit, merge or fast-forward of the trunk made by hand is refused unless every commit it adds to the first-parent line is a landing marker, the record land makes, a commit that only adds to the tracker data (a claim may also be rewritten or removed) or only closes items, naima init's commit, one that only switches the guard, or one with a Trunk-reason: trailer; a tip the upstream holds, a rewind, a ref created or deleted pass |
| [`changes`](#naima-changes) | coordination | print the release notes a range of commits makes, assembled from the change notes it adds to changes/, as Markdown: breaking changes first, then those that need an action, then features, behaviour changes and fixes, each with its text and what to do, and a Credits section last, as naima credits --markdown prints it; from the newest version tag (v…) to HEAD unless --from and --to say otherwise, in every repository of the project with a changes/config.json (the project itself, a submodule) unless --repo names one | nothing: it only prints; a change note that does not parse is named on stderr |
| [`prune`](#naima-prune) | coordination | list (or with --write remove) stale claim files: their branch is gone, or is the trunk, or merged into the trunk that carries the file, or every item they claim is closed; one only another ref carries is listed with that ref, to be dropped there. With --branch, delete a branch and its worktree, refusing one with unmerged commits that no archive/<branch> tag holds | the trunk is never pruned, and a branch with unmerged commits that no archive/<branch> tag holds is refused, and so is a worktree with anything uncommitted, inside its submodules too; a clean one is removed even when it holds a submodule; nothing is removed without --write |
| [`stale`](#naima-stale) | coordination | the work left behind: every branch, worktree and claim with no sign of life for staleAfter hours, or whose branch is gone or merged, with what it holds and the next step | nothing: it only reads; a branch counts as stale when its claim is stale (branch gone or merged into the trunk, or every item closed) or nothing happened on it for staleAfter hours (24 here) — no commit, step, session note or file changed; the next step is resume when anything is not committed, land when it is ahead of the trunk, up to date with it and holds open items, resume when it is behind, archive when no open item is claimed, drop when the trunk has all of it or the branch is gone |
| [`pass`](#naima-pass) | coordination | write this session's note (one new file), or list the newest | a session note is one new file: earlier ones are never rewritten; a note is refused without --ack when the project's active rules ask for an acknowledgement, and --ack is refused unless it carries every phrase they ask for |
| [`event`](#naima-event) | coordination | record an event the timeline cannot derive — a decision taken elsewhere, a build handed out, a policy, an outside fact — as one new file; everything else on `naima view timeline` is derived | an event has a YYYY-MM-DD date and a one-word kind, and is one new file; what the timeline derives is never recorded |
| [`diary`](#naima-diary) | coordination | the project's story, day by day and in order: events recorded with --kind diary, every decision with its reason, every artifact delivered, every session note; nothing stored but those files | nothing: it reads the records, the decisions, the artifacts and the session notes, and writes nothing |
| [`triage`](#naima-triage) | triage | coverage of the four fields; set them; list what needs a human; derive what the page proves | the four fields take only their declared values, through the write hooks; derive writes only with --write |
| [`gates`](#naima-gates) | gates | every gate, whoever declared it, and whether it holds; --check exits 1 if one does not | with --check, every listed gate holds: exit 1 if one does not |
| [`gate`](#naima-gate) | gates | declare a gate — a milestone, with a date and a version — put items on it or take them off, and show one; writes go to naima.json and to the items, validated, through the write hooks | writes to naima.json and to the items are validated and pass the write hooks |
| [`queue`](#naima-queue) | gates | open items on a gate, split by whose hands the proof needs; at its foot, the summary sections that stand beside the work, such as the metrics. With --role, one role's queue instead | nothing: it prints derived state, never stored |
| [`coverage`](#naima-coverage) | gates | each normative list the project declares — read from its source now, never copied — every entry with the test that proves it, or NO TEST | nothing: it reads each list from its source every time, never a copy, and marks an entry no test proves NO TEST |
| [`ready`](#naima-ready) | gates | the open items that wait on nothing still open -- every `blocked-by` target settled -- most urgent first: what can start now; on a gate, only its items | nothing: it prints derived state, never stored |
| [`order`](#naima-order) | gates | every open item in an order that puts it after everything it waits on (`blocked-by`), with its depth -- how many waits stand before it; items stuck on a cycle are listed apart | nothing: it prints derived state, never stored |
| [`epic`](#naima-epic) | epics | each epic with its progress — n of m closed, what it waits for and whose hands — or put items in an epic and take them out | only an epic groups items and never itself, and its status follows its items: setting it against them is refused |
| [`meeting`](#naima-meeting) | discussions | declare a meeting — who it needs, and a date or whenever they are present — put discussions on its agenda, and show the agenda | only a discussion goes on a meeting's agenda, and a meeting is written to naima.json validated, as the next load reads it |
| [`decide`](#naima-decide) | discussions | record the decision a discussion reached and mark it decided — a commit the trunk takes, during a meeting; a follow-up is filed only with the owner's yes | a discussion is decided only with its decision recorded; follow-up work is filed only with --consent, the owner's yes restated, and linked from the discussion |
| [`spec`](#naima-spec) | planning | each specification: its current version, its drafts, and the open items that follow it; or revise one into its next version | a revision is a new spec item, its next version, that supersedes the old one; the old version is kept as it was |
| [`decisions`](#naima-decisions) | planning | search the owner's decisions before asking: the settled ones whose title or page hold every word given, newest first | nothing: it only searches, so a settled question is looked up before it is asked again |
| [`confirm`](#naima-confirm) | planning | record the owner's confirmation of a proposed requirement, one someone other than the owner filed: it becomes stated, and gates count it from then on; the owner's yes, restated, is kept on the item | only a proposed requirement is confirmed, and only with the owner's words restated: an agent runs it after the owner said yes, never on its own judgement |
| [`model-first`](#naima-model-first) | planning | show or set how strictly the project applies model first (planning option modelFirst): strict, the rule a must; advisory, a should, with code that existed before the setting exempt unless rewritten and a new protocol or concurrency kept a must; deferred until a gate or a date the owner names, which files at once the todo that plans adopting model checking there | the setting is the owner's choice: an agent sets it only after the owner said which; deferring always names a gate or a date and files its todo |
| [`knowledge`](#naima-knowledge) | knowledge | print the established knowledge entries by kind, each with its source or evidence | nothing: it reads the knowledge entries and prints them; `naima check` holds what an entry must stand on |
| [`roles`](#naima-roles) | roles | every role: what it owns, what it refuses, the kinds and types on its queue, and how many open items are on it | nothing: it only reads; a role that refuses nothing is refused when the plugin loads |
| [`announce`](#naima-announce) | announce | the features that may be announced — user-facing, shipped, documented and checked by a person or end to end — major first: the source of release notes | nothing: it only lists, and only features user-facing, shipped, documented and checked by a person or end to end |
| [`credits`](#naima-credits) | announce | every attribution in use in the project — Naima itself, each plugin or stance loaded from outside Naima, what a plugin runs without installing it, and every tool a loaded plugin declares — each with its name, homepage, source, authors, licence and version, and what it fails to declare (provisional) | nothing: it only prints |
| [`loop`](#naima-loop) | loop | the non-stop loop on a target chosen before starting — a work list, an epic or a gate: done or not, the next agent work, the stop verdict, and once stopped the owner's ordered action list, each line saying why it is his | the loop runs only on a target chosen before starting — a work list, an epic or a gate —; with --check, exit 1 while it is not stopped |
| [`beta`](#naima-beta) | beta-markers | list what is marked as shipped without proof, and the state of each proof | nothing: it only reads |
| [`verify`](#naima-verify) | verifier | run the verifier of properties and attach each run as evidence, here or in a declared host's checkout | a property holds only with a run of its verifier on exactly what it has now, attached as evidence; every input is hashed by its committed content, a text file's CRLF line endings read as LF, so every checkout hashes alike; a model or input outside the project is refused; a conclusive run (holds or violated) already recorded on the same identity — every input's digest with the tool's version, and the options — is reused, not repeated, unless --force gives the reason to run it again; --tool-args passes only flags the verifier declares as leaving the verdict alone, recorded with the run; with --host, the run is made in the host's checkout, which writes nothing there, and kept here only when it was made on exactly what this checkout has |
| [`verifiers`](#naima-verifiers) | verifier | list the verifier adapters every plugin contributes | nothing: it only reads |
| [`equivalent`](#naima-equivalent) | verifier | compare a model with the earlier version its properties were verified on, modulo an equivalence, and carry each result over to the model as it is now when the two are equivalent: a refactoring proved without running its properties again | a result carries over only from a conclusive run on an earlier version of the model, with everything else it read unchanged — the property, the options, every other input, the tool's version — when the verifier finds the two versions equivalent and says the equivalence preserves the property; the carried run is recorded as such, naming the run it came from, the earlier version and the comparison |
| [`tools`](#naima-tools) | tools | the tools the loaded plugins declare, on this machine or a declared host: what is installed, missing or unavailable; show what an install would fetch; install one with consent into Naima's own directory, its download checked and the tool verified, never touching PATH or the system; remove one; print an installed program's path | an install fetches only the declared source, refuses a size or sha256 that differs, keeps nothing that fails its verification, and goes on only with consent — a yes on a terminal, or --consent with --by, recorded in the receipt; nothing is written outside the tools directory; a tool another installed tool needs is not removed |
| [`backup`](#naima-backup) | backup | the remote of each repository Naima relies on — the tracker's own, kept private beside the code, and the project's: say which have one; create a private GitHub repository with gh, after the owner's yes; add one the owner made by hand; record that the owner keeps one on this machine | a repository Naima relies on is never left without a remote unless the owner said so: the owner is asked once, at init or at the next update, and a no is recorded and recalled by naima hello |
| [`metrics`](#naima-metrics) | metrics | the project's metrics — each a name and the command or code measure that takes it — run, recorded per commit, held to a budget, a floor or a baseline, and read back along the commit timeline as a trend, a table or a chart; every number with the one it is compared to | numbers are recorded with the commit they measure; a ratcheted bound only tightens, and loosening one is refused without --because naming the item that says why |
| [`rules`](#naima-rules) | rules | print the project's active rules, must before should, each with its text and reason, ending with the line an agent must acknowledge back; or check that text carries every one (rules check-ack) | nothing: it only reads |
| [`reviewed`](#naima-reviewed) | rules | record that an agent reviewed a change against a rule verified by an agent (no check holds it): which rule, the item the change lands with, and what was checked; naima land shows the review, and notes a change to what such a rule covers that lands with none | the rule is an active rule verified by agent, the item exists, and what was checked is said; each review is one new file under rule-reviews/, landed with the change |
| [`run`](#naima-run) | long-work | start a long command detached — locally, or on a declared host through its own Naima — with a log, a progress file, a time budget and, on what it declares it creates, a disk budget, ending itself when one runs out; list the runs against their budgets, show one, stop one, or remove what one created | every run has a time budget, and is ended, its whole process group with it, when it runs out or its declared paths outgrow the disk budget; a declared path is never the root, the home directory, the repository or above it, nor holds a tracked file; a run is never cleaned while it runs; a remote run is always guarded, failing when it changes a tracked file; nothing starts on its own: a due long run is reported and filed, and starts only when a person or an agent runs it |
| [`wait`](#naima-wait) | long-work | block until a run started by naima run ends, or the timeout passes, saying how it goes meanwhile, then print its state, exit status, budgets, last progress line and the log's tail: found by its record, never by a process pattern | a wait is always bounded: it ends at its --timeout (default 10m) and says the run is still running, exiting 1, so waiting again is a decision; it exits 0 only for a run that succeeded |
| [`hooks`](#naima-hooks) | commit-hooks | the pre-commit hook and the companion rules it holds: list them, install the hook — tracked in the data directory, named by core.hooksPath once per clone — or uninstall it | the installed pre-commit hook runs the staged checks and the companion rules before every commit; install refuses to take over a core.hooksPath that is not Naima's unless --force |
| [`attach`](#naima-attach) | privacy | copy a file into an item's attachments with a record of whose it is: the owner's, only with their explicit yes restated in --consent, or your own with --own; a file holding a secret is refused | an owner's file is attached only with their yes restated in --consent, or the writer's own with --own; a file holding a secret, a hidden or path-like name, or a name already used is refused, and so is a text holding private infrastructure (a machine name, an IP address, a URI with a port, a home-directory path, the user's name, a word of the private list) unless --allow-private "<reason>" is given, which the item's notes record |
| [`adopt`](#naima-adopt) | adopt | adopt a board the project already keeps (a TODO.md, an issue list in markdown) as items, without losing a line: propose markers, split, audit, links — each a dry run until --write; the source is never deleted | no line of the source is lost and the source is never deleted; nothing is written without --write, and the only edit to the source is adding marker lines |
| [`docs`](#naima-docs) | docs | print the reference generated from the loaded manifests; write it, or check that a file matches it | with --check, the file is what the manifests generate and every loaded contribution is documented, this field included: exit 1 otherwise |

## Extension points

Every kind of contribution is an extension point: the core's own, and any a plugin declares. A plugin contributes to one under its id.

| Point | Declared by | What it is | Contributed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commands` | core | `naima <name>`: a command, with its usage, options and examples | core, trackers, coordination, triage, gates, epics, discussions, planning, knowledge, roles, announce, loop, beta-markers, verifier, tools, backup, ui, metrics, rules, long-work, commit-hooks, privacy, adopt, docs |
| `types` | core | item types: a directory of items, their statuses, and the status a new one starts in | core, trackers, epics, discussions, planning, knowledge, verifier, rules |
| `fields` | core | typed fields of an item's meta.json, and the types they apply to | core, trackers, triage, gates, discussions, planning, knowledge, roles, announce, verifier, rules, long-work, privacy, adopt, docs |
| `relations` | core | link relations between items, each naming its inverse | core, trackers, epics, discussions, planning, knowledge, verifier |
| `checks` | core | invariants `naima check` holds: a problem fails it, a note does not | core, trackers, coordination, triage, gates, epics, discussions, planning, knowledge, announce, beta-markers, verifier, metrics, rules, long-work, commit-hooks, privacy, docs |
| `views` | core | `naima view <name>`: a named rendering of derived state | coordination, triage, planning |
| `dirs` | core | directories under the tracker root a plugin owns that are not item types | core, coordination, metrics, rules, commit-hooks, adopt |
| `summary` | core | a block of `naima summary`; one marked `hello` is said by `naima hello` among what waits on the owner, and one with `goals(ctx)` says there where the project is going | core, trackers, coordination, triage, gates, epics, discussions, planning, beta-markers, verifier, backup, metrics, long-work |
| `guide` | core | a block `naima guide` prints first, inside a project, before the documentation pages | triage, verifier, rules |
| `rank` | core | an additive term of every item's urgency; lower is more urgent | triage, gates |
| `jobs` | core | a job the tick runs when it is due, once an hour or once a day, whichever naima process wins it; what it finds is shown to the owner as messages | long-work |
| `extends` | core | additive changes to another plugin's type — statuses (an existing one only with its category), traits, transitions — or field — enum values, more types or traits it applies to | discussions, knowledge, roles |
| `hooks` | core | hooks on every item write: `beforeWrite(write, ctx)` may change or refuse it, `afterWrite(write, ctx)` sees it done; `beforeText(text, ctx)` may refuse a write of free text or a file that is not an item's (a session note, an event, an attachment) or add to its record | core, coordination, triage, epics, discussions, planning, knowledge, verifier, privacy |
| `setup` | core | what a plugin puts in place in the project's clone where it is missing (a git hook, a file), run by `naima init` and `naima update` after their own work: `install(ctx) → lines`, each said | coordination, planning, backup, metrics |
| `agent-hooks` | core | a hook the agent tool runs, which Naima installs in the tool's settings beside its own at `naima init`, `naima update` and `naima stance adopt`, and removes once the plugin is gone: `name`, `says`, `tool` (the agent tool, by adapter id), `event` and optionally `matcher` in that tool's terms, and `command`, the naima command it runs as a list of words |  |
| `migrations` | core | a plugin's own data migrations, in order from its format 1, run by `naima update` after the core's | gates |
| `credits` | core | what a plugin runs or builds on without installing it (a program found on PATH, say), credited by `naima credits`: name, homepage, source, authors, license, version (provisional) | verifier |
| `landing-reports` | coordination | what `naima land` checks before a branch lands and reports once it has: `name`, `says`, and `refuses(ctx, { branch, from, to, changed }) → lines`, what fails on the branch, any line refusing the landing with no flag to let it through; `blocks(ctx, landing) → lines`, what the landing changed whose proofs are not current, any line refusing the landing unless --stale-proofs gives the reason; or `report(ctx, landing) → lines`, printed after it, never blocking; `changed` is every file the landing changed, from the project root | verifier, rules |
| `gates` | gates | a named release or merge condition, backed by items: `title`, `says`, `decides`, `evaluate(ctx) → { holds, blocking, owed }`; `inFullSuite` makes it part of the full suite a release gate (`fullSuite`) requires | verifier |
| `roles` | roles | a role of the company of agents: `title`, what it `owns`, what it `refuses` (never empty), the `kinds` and `types` on its queue, and `queue(ctx)`, its open items most urgent first | roles |
| `verifiers` | verifier | an adapter to a formal-methods tool: `verify({ model, property, options }, ctx) → { verdict, output, counterexample?, details? }`; optionally `inputs(request, ctx)`, every file a run reads, and `version(ctx)`, the tool's version, both kept in the run's digest; `toolArgs`, the flags `naima verify --tool-args` may pass, which never change the verdict; and `equivalences` with `compare({ before, after, equivalence }, ctx) → { verdict, output, counterexample?, details? }` and `preserves({ property, options, equivalence }, ctx)`, for `naima equivalent` | verifier, verifier-mcrl2 |
| `tools` | tools | a tool a plugin needs, which `naima tools install` installs into Naima's own directory: name, exact version, licence, homepage, source and authors (its attribution, which `naima credits` prints), programs, how an install is verified, and per platform a source (url, size, sha256, format) or the answer saying why there is none | backup, verifier-mcrl2 |
| `ui-views` | ui | a view the provisional window shows as a tab, or as a panel of its first screen: `name` (its path), `title`, `says`, `order` (lower first, 0 when absent), `panel` (true: on the first screen, not a tab), `render(params, ctx) → { data, html, css? }`, rendered at each request | coordination, triage, gates, ui, metrics |
| `metric-kinds` | metrics | how a metric's number is read from its run: `read({ exit, stdout, stderr, seconds }, metric) → number \| { error }`, `readsExit` | metrics |
| `metrics` | metrics | a named measurement: `run` (a program and its arguments) and `kind`, a code `measure`, a test `suite`'s number or a `file`'s; a bound — `atMost`, `atLeast` or `equals` — and `better` |  |
| `code-measures` | metrics | a code-quality number taken in process from the files: `measure({ files, source }, metric) → number \| { error }`, with its `unit` and `better` | metrics |
| `code-languages` | metrics | a language code measures read: `extensions`, `code`, `comments`, `quotes`, `strip(text)` when the generic comment scan cannot read it, and `functions(stripped) → [{ name, line, lines, complexity }]` when it can find them | metrics |
| `test-formats` | metrics | how a test suite's machine-readable output is read: `parse(text) → [{ name, file, result, seconds, message }] \| { error }` | metrics |
| `test-suites` | metrics | a test suite: `run` (a program and its arguments), the `format` its report is in, and where the `report` is |  |
| `rules` | rules | a rule a plugin ships, active in every project that loads it beside the project's own rules items: one Markdown file per rule in a folder the plugin names (`contributes: { rules: "rules/" }`), its front matter `name`, `title`, `audience`, `strength`, and optionally `ack`, `enforcedBy`, `verifiedBy`, `covers` (the files it is about, for a rule an agent verifies) and `when`, its body the rule and a section `## Why`; a project retires one with the rules plugin's `retire` option | coordination, planning, long-work, working-rules |

## core

Items, fields, links and the invariants every project has.

Its contributions' qualified ids are `core/<name>`.

An item is a directory under `<tracker>/<TYPE>/<slug>/`: `README.md` for the prose, `meta.json` for the fields, `attachments/` for the evidence. `meta.json` always holds `id` (a permanent uuid), `title` and `status` (one the item's type declares), and optionally `links`, a list of `{ rel, id }`. The slug may change; the id may not, and links hold ids. An item reference on the command line is an id, `type/slug`, a slug, or a fragment of a slug that matches one item. Fields are typed by the plugin that declares them — `string`, `strings` (comma-separated on the command line), `date` (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD), `enum` (values in rank order), `boolean`, `number`, `object` (a JSON object, written as JSON on the command line) — and unknown fields are kept and not checked. Only one direction of a link is stored; the inverse is derived when read. Boards, queues, gate states and summaries are derived when asked and never stored. An item is open or done by its status's category; urgency is the sum of every plugin's rank terms, and done items sink. A check's finding can be waived when it is accepted rather than fixed: `naima waive <check> <subject> --reason "<why>" --as <who>` writes one file under `waivers/` naming the check, the subject, the reason, who and when. A waived finding is not a failure; every `naima check` lists the waivers in use as notes, and notes a waiver whose subject no longer exists or no longer fails. Only a check that names the subject of its findings can be waived.

### naima init

Make the git repository around the program a Naima project, as its first run does by itself: beside the program, a git clone of Naima at naima-tracker/naima/, create naima-data/naima.json, locked to the clone's origin and its HEAD, which must be on the origin's main — with the release's version and checksum when the installer unpacked a release into it —, and the tracker folder's README.md and .gitignore; print the line that keeps the program out of each host tool configuration it finds (deno.json, tsconfig.json, .prettierignore); and write what makes an agent run naima hello at the start of every session: the line that tells agents where Naima is and to run it, into the host's AGENTS.md, else the first entry file it has, else a new AGENTS.md, and the hooks of each agent tool the project uses that has them (naima.json's agents; absent it, those whose files the project holds and the one Naima runs inside): a session-start hook that runs naima hello, and a turn-end hook that runs the tick when the agent ends its turn; for a repository that is public on GitHub, offer the topic naima, for the agent to ask the owner before adding it (never for a private one); nothing else outside naima-tracker/ is touched unless --write-excludes is given.

**Enforces**: The program is locked to a commit of its source's main, with nothing uncommitted; outside the tracker folder, only the pointer line, the session-start hooks and, with --write-excludes, the exclusion lines are written.

```sh
naima init [--private-tracker
naima --tracker <url> [--private-url]
naima --tracker-inside
naima --remote-private] [--write-excludes] [--no-session-hook]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--private-tracker` |  | keep the tracker private beside the code: naima-data/ becomes a git repository of its own, created on this machine with no remote, ignored by the project's git, and naima-tracker/tracker.json, committed with the code, says so; the two repositories' commits are paired by Tracker: and Code: trailers (a commit-msg hook in both) and their branches by name. A tracker already committed with the code is moved there with its history (git filter-branch of the code's trunk to naima-data/; the code's repository stops tracking it in one commit, its files left in place, nothing deleted), and a todo is filed, once, at the highest priority, to sweep the tracker for private and confidential information. Without any of these options, init keeps the tracker inside a project with no remote, or a private one; it stops when the remote is public, saying the tracker must be private, and with the question to ask the owner when its visibility cannot be told (GitHub's public API, asked without credentials) |
| `--tracker` |  | like --private-tracker, from an existing tracker repository: naima-data/ becomes a git clone of the one at <url>, whose address tracker.json records |
| `--private-url` |  | with --tracker: keep the tracker's address out of tracker.json, in this clone's git config (naima.tracker) |
| `--tracker-inside` |  | commit the tracker with the code when the visibility of its remote cannot be told: the owner's answer to init's question that the remote is private, recorded as --remote-private records it; refused when the remote is public |
| `--remote-private` |  | in a project that has its tracker: record the owner's answer that the tracker's remotes whose visibility cannot be told are private, in naima-data/naima.json's privateRemotes, by a hash of each address, so the question is not asked again; refused for a remote GitHub says is public |
| `--write-excludes` |  | also write those lines into the host's own files: deno.json and tsconfig.json when they are plain JSON, .prettierignore; a file with comments is left to be edited by hand |
| `--no-session-hook` |  | install no agent tool's session-start hook: only the pointer line is written; naima check notes the hook missing, and naima update installs it |

Examples:

```sh
naima init
naima init --private-tracker
naima init --remote-private
naima init --tracker git@example.invalid:me/tracker.git --private-url
naima init --write-excludes
naima init --no-session-hook
```

### naima update

Move the lock to the newest release of the source, or to the version or commit --to names: download the release's archive, check it against its SHA-256 and against the commit its tag names, and record the version and checksum with the commit (a source that publishes no releases, or --main, follows the head of its main instead; a lock that still names a commit of main moves to the newest release once, and says so; a commit of main past the newest release stays until a newer release; with no network the lock stays where it is, and says why); say what changes (the commits, the change notes they add — breaking first, then those that ask an action —, the data formats, the rules added or removed, the options it no longer reads), fetch it into the program, check it out, rename and remove options in naima.json as the change notes say and remove those it reads nowhere, each said with its value, and record the new commit; moving forward, the new Naima finishes: it migrates the data if its format moved, names the rules agents acknowledge again, runs naima check, and files an item in the type with the trait follow-up for each problem or note that is new since the commit before; writes, and says, what makes agents run naima hello at every session start where it is missing — the pointer line, rewritten when it does not say so, and each session-start hook as naima init installs them; all as one change to commit; the only command, with rollback, that moves the lock; with --mode, set what a session start does about a newer Naima.

**Enforces**: The lock moves only to a release whose archive matches its checksum and its tag's commit, or, for a source without releases or with --main, to a commit of the source's main, with the data migrated forward in the same change; never back past a migration, which runs forward only; a source naima.json names other than the program's origin is refused, by every command, until --accept-source.

```sh
naima update [--check
naima --to <version|commit>
naima --main
naima --pre
naima --mode off|check|update
naima --accept-source]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--check` |  | only say whether a newer release exists (for a source without releases, whether its main has moved past the locked commit), and what it changes — and rehearse it: its own naima check, run on the project from a temporary copy of it, writing nothing, says what would newly fail or be noted; exit 1 when it has moved |
| `--to` |  | move the lock to this release (1.2.0 or v1.2.0), or to this commit of the source's main, forward or back; back across a data format is refused, naming the commit to revert; the option updates is removed when that commit does not know it, and said |
| `--main` |  | follow the head of the source's main rather than its releases, as for Naima's own development or a fork that publishes no releases; the lock then names a commit, with no version, and is not counted as an install of a release |
| `--pre` |  | include pre-releases (1.2.0-rc.1) when choosing the newest release; a project that already runs a pre-release includes them without it |
| `--mode` | `check` | set naima.json's updates, what naima hello does at a session start: off (nothing asked of the source), check (say when a newer Naima exists), update (say what it changes, and offer it; applied only after the owner's yes) |
| `--accept-source` |  | trust the source naima.json now names, after reviewing why it changed: every other command refuses to run a program from a source other than its origin; points the program's origin at the new source, checks out the locked commit, and moves nothing else |

Examples:

```sh
naima update --check
naima update
naima update --to 1.2.0
naima update --to 0123456789ab
naima update --main
naima update --mode update
naima update --accept-source
```

### naima rollback

Move the lock back to the one naima.json recorded before it, found in its git history, as one change to commit: what update --to does with that commit, its version and checksum recorded again when it named a release.

**Enforces**: The lock goes back only to a commit that reads the data's formats: a migration is undone by reverting its commit, never by running an older Naima on newer data.

```sh
naima rollback
```

Examples:

```sh
naima rollback
```

### naima hello

What an agent says first in a session: the banner (I'm Naima, the No-guesswork Artificial Intelligence Meta-Agent, active in this repository, with its version and commit); then, as naima.json's updates says, whether a newer Naima exists and, under update, what it changes and its rehearsal, as update --check says them; then where the project is going, as the plugins say it, such as the nearest gate with a due date and the next release, each with its verdict as naima gates gives it; then, one line each, what waits on the owner's decision, such as a long run that is due, never started, or that nothing does; then what it offers on request: what the plugins offer, such as generating code from a model the project has, then what Naima is and its documentation, an update check, an update after the owner's yes; last, the offer to explain what Naima can do from the basics (docs/guide/the-basics.md). Under --hook, the agent is told to open its first reply with the introduction, its name in bold, and how to explain the basics.

**Enforces**: It never moves the lock nor starts a run; it asks the source only when updates is check or update, and records that check as the day's, and the session it starts (naima origin), in the tick's state outside the repository; the only thing it may write in the project is an urgent message the tick raises.

```sh
naima hello [--hook <tool>] [--session <id>]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--session` |  | the id of the session it starts, which every write in this worktree records until the next hello (naima origin); without it, the agent tool's own when its hook is given one, else a new one: the day and eight hex digits |
| `--hook` |  | print the greeting as the session-start hook of that agent tool wants it, named as naima.json's agents names it: the greeting for the owner to see directly, and what the agent is to say first, in the form the tool's adapter gives (src/core/adapters/) |

Examples:

```sh
naima hello
naima hello --hook <tool>
```

### naima tick

Run the tick now, as every command does before its own work: each job that is due — the update check once a day, unless updates is off; the jobs plugins contribute, such as the due long runs once an hour — run by whichever naima process wins it, a failed one retried an hour later, a week of failed update checks raising an urgent message; then say what is due to the owner, each message once, an urgent one once an hour until the owner acknowledges it (naima messages). Every other command says them after its own output, on standard error, one line each: NAIMA-MESSAGE, a space, and the message as a JSON object with the keys id, level (info, warning or urgent), text and ack, where ack is the command that acknowledges it, or null for a message said once.

**Enforces**: No lock: every decision is a file created only if it does not exist, kept outside the repository in the clone's git directory, so any number of naima processes, in any worktree of the clone, run each due job once; nothing is applied and no long work starts: it finds and says.

```sh
naima tick [--json] [--hook <tool>]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | print the jobs run here and the messages to show as JSON |
| `--hook` |  | run as the turn-end hook of that agent tool, named as naima.json's agents names it: when a message is due, print what keeps the agent from ending its turn and tells it what to tell or ask the owner, in the form the tool's adapter gives; nothing otherwise; it never fails |

Examples:

```sh
naima tick
naima tick --json
naima tick --hook <tool>
```

### naima subagent

Run as the sub-agent-start hook of that agent tool, named as naima.json's agents names it: put the project's rules for agents, as naima rules --audience agents prints them, in the starting sub-agent's context, in the form the tool's adapter gives, and mark, by the sub-agent's id, that it has them, so the tool's guard lets its calls through; the guard holds the calls of a sub-agent with no mark until it runs naima rules, and the hook on its stop sends one that never had them back to read them (docs/agents/read-the-project-rules.md).

**Enforces**: It never fails and never blocks a sub-agent from starting: a project that does not open, or an input with no agent id, prints nothing and leaves the guard to hold the sub-agent until it reads the rules; the mark is kept outside the repository, in the clone's git directory.

```sh
naima subagent --hook <tool>
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--hook` |  | the agent tool whose sub-agent-start hook runs it, named as naima.json's agents names it |

Examples:

```sh
naima subagent --hook <tool>
```

### naima plugin

Turn a plugin on or off, or set one of its options, in naima.json's plugins table — validated the way the project is validated on every load, instead of a hand-edit of the file.

**Enforces**: A name must be a first-party plugin (loaded or opt-in) or one the table already names with its own source; an option set on one whose options are known here must be one it declares; the whole file is re-validated before it is written, so nothing a later load would refuse ever reaches disk.

```sh
naima plugin enable <name>
naima plugin disable <name>
naima plugin set <name> <option>=<value>...
naima plugin show [<name>]
```

Examples:

```sh
naima plugin enable verifier-mcrl2
naima plugin set verifier-mcrl2 bin=/usr/local/bin
naima plugin disable rule-templates
naima plugin show verifier-mcrl2
naima plugin show
```

### naima stances

List the stances available to adopt — plugins of the kind stance, each a set of authored choices and rules a project takes as a whole — with what each says of itself, marking those this project has adopted; for now they are the repositories named naima-stance-<name> of the naima-project organisation on GitHub, asked of GitHub's public API without credentials; with no network, it says it cannot reach it.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it only reads.

```sh
naima stances
```

Examples:

```sh
naima stances
```

### naima stance

Adopt a stance, show the ones adopted, or list a stance's examples. adopt <name> resolves the name to its repository, github.com/naima-project/naima-stance-<name>, pins the commit at the head of its default branch in naima.json's plugins as stance-<name> (its module plugin/index.mjs), loads it, and runs its adoption when it declares one: its own command stance-<name> with adopt, given the arguments after the name; adopting again moves the pin to the newest commit. status shows each adopted stance, its pinned commit, and whether a newer one exists. examples <name> lists the example paths an adopted stance declares, each with where it is in its checkout, from the project's root.

**Enforces**: A stance is pinned by commit, as every plugin from git is, and the whole file is re-validated before it is written; what is adopted must declare the kind stance, or naima.json is put back as it was.

```sh
naima stance adopt <name> [<arguments of its adoption>...]
naima stance status
naima stance examples <name>
```

Examples:

```sh
naima stance adopt ui
naima stance adopt ui --mood dusk
naima stance status
naima stance examples ui
```

### naima new

Open an item.

**Enforces**: Every field is validated against its type's declarations before the item exists, and every write hook runs: a typo or a refusal leaves nothing behind; an archive type takes no new item.

```sh
naima new <type> "<title>" [--section <s>] [--set field=value]... [--asked-by <role>] [--by <who>] [--from <item>] [--dedupe]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--asked-by` | `agent` | who asked for it, recorded in its origin: owner only for what the owner said, asked, reported or decided; coordinator or worker for what that agent asked; agent for what an agent found on its own; person:<name> for someone else |
| `--by` | `git's user.name` | who files it, recorded in its origin |
| `--from` |  | the item it was derived from, recorded in its origin: a bug found while working on a feature |
| `--section` |  | the heading the item is grouped under on its board |
| `--set` |  | a field=value pair to set on the new item; repeatable |
| `--dedupe` |  | print items of the same type with a similar title before writing; never blocks |

Examples:

```sh
naima new bugs "Export drops the alpha channel"
naima new tests "Export keeps the alpha channel" --set runBy=agent --section export
naima new todos "Retry export on timeout" --dedupe
naima new requirements "Export keeps the alpha channel" --asked-by owner
naima new bugs "Export crashes on an empty layer" --from export-keeps
```

List what Naima has to tell the owner: the urgent messages not yet acknowledged, which the tick shows at most once an hour, then what it said once, such as a newer Naima; with ack, the owner acknowledges a message, which stops it being shown, in every worktree and, once the tracker is committed, on every machine.

**Enforces**: A message is acknowledged only by the owner's command, never on their behalf; an acknowledgement is never undone.


| Option | Default | What it does |

### naima origin

Say the session this worktree is in; with a session id, list what that session filed (each with who asked) and every other item it changed, to review a session that drifted and undo it item by item; with --backfill, give every item with no origin one inferred from git; with --set, settle who asked for an item, such as one the backfill left unknown.

**Enforces**: An origin is never changed but for who asked, and only through --set, which keeps the rest as it was and records each correction in the origin: what it was, who set it, when; the backfill writes only to items with none, marks each inferred: true with askedBy unknown, for the owner to settle in a review; the session's log is read from outside the repository and never committed.

**Progress**: none — the backfill asks git once per item, with no total known to git; instead, It prints one line per item it gives an origin.

```sh
naima origin [<session>] [--json]
naima origin --backfill [--dry-run]
naima origin --set <item> --asked-by <owner|coordinator|worker|agent|unknown|person:<name>> [--by <name>]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | print the review as JSON: the session, the items it filed, the items it changed |
| `--backfill` |  | give each item with no origin the one git gives: the commit that added its meta.json, its author and date, the branch of the landing marker that brought it in; inferred: true, askedBy unknown |
| `--dry-run` |  | with --backfill: say what it would write, and write nothing |
| `--set` |  | the item whose origin says who asked to set, as --asked-by gives it; the correction is recorded in its origin |
| `--asked-by` |  | with --set: who asked, a role (owner, coordinator, worker, agent, unknown) or person:<name> |
| `--by` |  | with --set: who makes the correction, as it is recorded; absent, git's user.name |

Examples:

```sh
naima origin
naima origin 2026-10-27-1a2b3c4d
naima origin 2026-10-27-1a2b3c4d --json
naima origin --backfill --dry-run
naima origin --backfill
naima origin --set bugs/export-crashes --asked-by owner
naima origin --set bugs/export-crashes --asked-by "person:Ada"
```

### type: messages

Messages: what Naima has to tell the owner and waits on them to read, such as an update check failing for days: created by the tick, acknowledged by the owner. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/messages/`; a new one starts as `unread`; it is an archive: items arrive by being moved there, never by being opened.

Traits: `messages`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unread` | open |  | raised, and not yet acknowledged by the owner: an urgent one is shown at most once an hour |
| `acknowledged` | done |  | the owner has read it: naima messages ack <id> |

Moves allowed: `acknowledged` → ; a status not named moves to any.

**Fields**

| Field | Kind | Applies to | Meaning | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `section` | string | every type | the heading the item is grouped under on its board |  |
| `created` | date | every type | when the item was opened |  |
| `tags` | strings | every type | free labels a person puts on an item |  |
| `origin` | object | every type | where the item comes from, written once by naima new and never changed but for who asked: { askedBy: owner, coordinator, worker, agent, person (with person: the name) or unknown; filedBy: { name, role }; session: the session it was filed in; on: the instant; branch; from: the id of the item it was derived from }, with inferred: true and commit when naima origin --backfill read it from git, and corrected: [{ was, by, on }] for each time naima origin --set changed who asked |  |
| `level` | enum | any type tagged `messages` | how much a message weighs: info and warning are said once, urgent is shown once an hour until acknowledged | `info` worth knowing; `warning` worth acting on; `urgent` the owner should know now: shown once an hour until acknowledged |
| `ready` | object | every type | the owner's approval of the work, as the close of a meeting records it: { on: the day, start: true when the owner said to start it now, meeting, decisions: the ids of the discussions it carries, consent: the owner's yes restated }; an open item with one is on the ready queue |  |

**Link relations** — only the direction written is stored; the inverse is derived when read.

| Relation | Inverse | Reads as |
|---|---|---|
| `relates-to` | `relates-to` | is related to |
| `duplicate-of` | `duplicate-of` | describes the same thing as |
| `blocks` | `blocked-by` | must be resolved before |
| `blocked-by` | `blocks` | waits on |

**Checks**, run by `naima check`

| Check | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `readable` | every item directory has a README.md and a meta.json that parses to an object whose id, title and status are strings; no symbolic link or _-prefixed directory sits unread among the items |
| `identity` | every item has a permanent uuid, a title and a status its type declares; ids are unique |
| `fields` | every declared field holds a value of its declared kind |
| `values` | every value of a field with an open list of values — area or kind, once the project declares their values — is on its list; a value off it is a note naming the items that hold it, which are never rewritten |
| `links` | every link uses a declared relation and names an existing item other than its own |
| `layout` | every directory under the tracker root belongs to an item type or a plugin |
| `duplicates` | items of one type with the same title are linked as duplicates, or reported |
| `entry-pointers` | every agent-harness entry file naima.json configures (entryFiles; sensible defaults absent it) names no path or link, plain-text or markdown, that is missing from disk |
| `session-start` | an agent is told to run naima hello at the start of every session: an entry file holds the pointer line, which says so, and each agent tool the project uses (naima.json's agents; absent it, those whose files the project holds and the one Naima runs inside) that has a session-start hook has it installed; each one missing is noted, with the naima update that adds it — or, after an update that moved the lock and could not write them, one note that the update is unfinished; and each hook a plugin contributes is installed as it is, and none is left of a plugin gone |
| `unread-options` | every option naima.json's plugins table sets is one its loaded plugin declares: an option no plugin reads any more is noted, by name |
| `tracker-private` | the tracker is not exposed: when it is committed with the code, the code repository's origin is not public; when it is a repository of its own, none of its remotes is public — a remote on this disk, or none, is private; a GitHub remote is asked of GitHub's public API at most once a day, the answer remembered in the tracker repository's git config; one whose visibility cannot be told is noted with the question for the owner, until the owner's answer is recorded (naima init --remote-private) |
| `one-format` | no item is still in a shape a format migration, the core's or a plugin's own, replaced: a tracker never mixes formats |

**Directories** it owns under the tracker root: `waivers/`.

**Summary sections**: `items`.

**Write hooks**, run on every item write

| Hook | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status-moves` | a status moves only to one its type's transitions allow from the status it has; a status the transitions do not name moves to any, and --force takes the move on |
| `notes-append-only` | a write of an item's prose keeps its Notes section as it was and may only add after it; --force takes a rewrite on |
| `private-infrastructure` | a write of an item's title, fields or prose that adds a machine name, an IP address, a URI with a port, a home-directory path, the user's name or a word of the private list is refused, each finding listed with the placeholder to write instead; --allow-private "<reason>" lets a deliberate mention through and records the reason in the item's notes |
| `origin-once` | every new item records its origin (who asked, in what role, who filed it, the session, the instant, the branch, the item it came from) and no later write changes or drops it; every write in a session is logged, outside the repository, for naima origin |

## trackers

Bugs, todos, features, tests, and the archive of closed bugs.

Its contributions' qualified ids are `trackers/<name>`.

Three words that are not synonyms:

- **fixed** — the code change exists: `fixedOn` is set. Nothing is proven.
- **resolved** — fixed, and proven by an item that `verifies` it and whose status `proves` (a passed test, a property that holds).
- **closed** — resolved, and moved to `closed/` by `naima close`, carrying its proof.

A todo whose work is a judgement with no code, a review or a decision (its `kind` says which), has nothing to fix and no test to pass. Once its status is `done` or `dropped`, `naima close <item> --reason "<what was settled, and where it is written>"` archives it without a proof. The reason is kept in `closedBecause`, and `naima check` lists every such item as a note, `closed-without-proof`, so nothing is closed this way unseen.

"How many bugs are left" means the unfixed count; `naima bugs` never adds the three together.

`fixedOn` applies to every type tagged `fixable` — bugs, todos, features and the archive here, and any other plugin's or project's type that carries the tag.

An item whose proof needs a person says why in `humanBecause`. Only a judgement, a reserved decision, a credential or a physical act makes something a person's: needing the running software makes it `agent-hands`, not `human`.

## The evidence ranking

Not all evidence is worth the same. From strongest to weakest, the values of a test's `evidenceKind`:

1. `owner-gesture` — the owner performed the gesture and saw the result
2. `observation` — a screenshot, a log line or a number, kept with the item
3. `live-read` — the live state, read by tooling: a query, an API call, the running program's own answer
4. `diff` — a before-and-after comparison: counts, sizes, outputs
5. `inspection` — the code looks right — which proves nothing

No number without its comparison: a count, a timing or a size proves something only beside the value it is compared with — before and after, expected and seen.

A regression test is one that `verifies` a bug. It proves the fix only if it was seen failing first, on the code before the fix: red, then green. `redSeen` records the day it was seen red, and the page's notes say how. `naima check` notes a passed regression test with no `redSeen`, and a passed test whose evidence is `inspection`.

## Stale pages

A page can outlive its answer. Two notes, never failures, find it: an open item's unticked `- [ ]` clause that names a test which has since passed, as `tests/<slug>` or as "the linked test" once every item verifying it has passed — `unticked-clause-names-passed-test`; and an open test marked `runBy: agent` whose page, below its title, excuses it with a resource being held — `test-excuses-itself`, matching the phrases in the option `excusePhrases`. Each can be weighed, or switched off, under `plugins.trackers.checks`.

Options, each with the default it takes when nothing sets it:

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `excusePhrases` | `["held by","was held","is held","in use by","locked by","busy","unavailable"]` | the phrases (any case) by which an open agent's test says it could not run because something was held; test-excuses-itself notes them |

### naima close

Archive a resolved item: fixed, and proven by an item that has passed; or a finished review or decision, with the reason.
