**Enforces**: An item is archived only when fixed and proven: fixedOn set and a verified-by item that has passed, with every write hook agreeing; --force takes a hook's refusal on, for the one who owns the evidence. --reason closes, without fixedOn, proof or commit, only a todo whose kind is review or decision and whose status is done or dropped; the reason is kept in closedBecause and naima check lists it.

```sh
naima close <item> [--force] [--reason "<why>"]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--force` |  | close it although a write hook refuses — for the one who owns the evidence, say an item this branch claims whose proof someone else performed |
| `--reason` |  | close a todo whose work is a judgement with no code — kind review or decision, its status done or dropped — without a proof: what was settled and where it is written, kept in closedBecause and listed by naima check as closed-without-proof |

Examples:

```sh
naima close export-drops
naima close export-drops --force
naima close review-last-two-days --reason "each change reviewed with the owner; the decisions are in the item's notes"
```

### naima bugs

How many bugs have no code written, and how many are fixed but unproven.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it only counts.

```sh
naima bugs
```

Examples:

```sh
naima bugs
```

### type: bugs

Bugs: something that is broken. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/bugs/`; a new one starts as `open`.

Traits: `fixable`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | open |  | nothing on the page has been done |
| `partial` | open |  | some of it has, and the page says what is left |
| `wontfix` | done |  | deliberately not fixed; the reason is on the page |

### type: todos

Todos: work that is not a defect: a task, a decision, a tidy-up. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/todos/`; a new one starts as `open`.

Traits: `fixable`, `follow-up`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | open |  | not started |
| `partial` | open |  | started; the page says what is left |
| `done` | done |  | finished |
| `dropped` | done |  | deliberately not done; the reason is on the page |

### type: features

Features: what the software does, or is asked to do. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/features/`; a new one starts as `requested`.

Traits: `fixable`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requested` | open |  | asked for; no code exists |
| `planned` | open |  | agreed and scheduled |
| `shipped` | done |  | on the trunk, with its documentation |
| `withdrawn` | done |  | decided against |

### type: tests

Tests: a gesture that proves something, and its result. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/tests/`; a new one starts as `open`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | open |  | not yet performed |
| `partial` | open |  | performed in part |
| `failed` | open | refutes | performed, and what it proves does not hold |
| `passed` | done | proves | performed, and it holds; the page carries the measurement |
| `withdrawn` | done |  | no longer applies: what it would prove was reversed; the page says by what |

### type: closed

Closed: the archive: resolved items, each with its proof. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/closed/`; a new one starts as `closed`; it is an archive: items arrive by being moved there, never by being opened.

Traits: `fixable`, `archive`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `closed` | done |  | fixed, proven, archived |

**Fields**

| Field | Kind | Applies to | Meaning | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fixedOn` | date | any type tagged `fixable` | when the code landed; absent means unfixed |  |
| `closedOn` | date | closed | when the item was archived |  |
| `closedFrom` | string | closed | the type the item was archived from |  |
| `closedBecause` | string | closed | why an item was closed without a proof: a todo of kind review or decision, closed by naima close --reason |  |
| `runBy` | enum | tests, bugs, todos | who can perform the proving gesture — the instrument, not the effort | `agent` settled by a command: a unit test, a grep, an API call; `agent-hands` settled by an agent driving the running software; `human` needs a person: a judgement of how it looks, a physical act, a reserved decision; `build` needs an artifact nobody here makes: a signed build, a second machine |
| `humanBecause` | enum | tests, bugs, todos | why only a person can perform the proof, when runBy is human | `judgement` how it looks, sounds or feels: no instrument can settle it; `decision` a decision reserved to the owner; `credential` a secret, an account or a signature only a person holds; `physical` a physical act or a machine only a person has at hand |
| `evidenceKind` | enum | tests | what the test's evidence is, from the ranking: strongest first | `owner-gesture` the owner performed the gesture and saw the result; `observation` a screenshot, a log line or a number, kept with the item; `live-read` the live state, read by tooling: a query, an API call, the running program's own answer; `diff` a before-and-after comparison: counts, sizes, outputs; `inspection` the code looks right — which proves nothing |
| `redSeen` | date | tests | the day a regression test was seen failing on the code before the fix: red, then green |  |
| `area` | string | every type | where it lives: the surface somebody would have open while working on it |  |
| `kind` | string | every type | the mode of work it demands: code, decision, research, writing… |  |
| `commits` | strings | any type tagged `fixable` | the git commit hashes that fixed it, each reachable from the trunk — or "legacy" on an item closed before this field existed, set once by migration, never retrofitted by guessing |  |

**Link relations** — only the direction written is stored; the inverse is derived when read.

| Relation | Inverse | Reads as |
|---|---|---|
| `verifies` | `verified-by` | is the gesture that proves |
| `verified-by` | `verifies` | is proven by |

**Checks**, run by `naima check`

| Check | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `partial-says-what-is-left` | a partial item carries at least one unticked `- [ ]` clause |
| `proven-but-open` | an open item whose proof has passed is reported so it can be closed |
| `fix-names-its-gesture` | a fixed item names the gesture that would prove it |
| `closed-carries-proof` | every archived item is verified by an item that has passed, unless it was closed with a reason as a review or a decision |
| `closed-without-proof` | every item closed with a reason instead of a proof (a todo of kind review or decision, naima close --reason) is listed as a note with its reason |
| `human-says-why` | an open item whose proof needs a person (runBy human) says why in humanBecause |
| `commits-are-real` | every hash an item's commits field names is a commit git has |
| `closed-names-its-commits` | an item closed on or after 2026-10-01 names a commit reachable from the trunk, unless it was closed with a reason as a review or a decision |
| `regression-test-saw-red` | a passed test that verifies a bug records the day it was seen failing first, in redSeen |
| `inspection-proves-nothing` | a passed test whose evidenceKind is inspection is noted: reading the code is no evidence |
| `passed-test-carries-evidence` | a passed test an agent performed by driving the running software (runBy agent-hands) carries what shows it passed, an attachment of what was run and what it printed; one with none is noted |
| `unticked-clause-names-passed-test` | an open item's unticked clause that names a test which has passed — as tests/<slug>, or as its linked test once every item verifying it has passed — is noted: tick it, or reopen the test |
| `test-excuses-itself` | an open test marked runBy agent whose page says a resource was held (the option excusePhrases) is noted: an agent's gesture waits on no one |

**Summary sections**: `bugs`.

## coordination

Claims and session notes, one file per session, recombined from every branch; the timeline, derived from the items and git.

Its contributions' qualified ids are `coordination/<name>`.

No session writes a file another session writes. A claim is one file per branch, `claims/<uuid>.json`; a session note is one file per session, `passes/<date>-<uuid>.md`. Both are written on the writer's own branch and never staged or committed by the tool: commit them with the work. `claims`, `pass --list` and `summary` recombine them at read time from every local branch — the trunk, every branch not merged into it, whatever each worktree stands on — each read from the disk of the worktree that stands on it, uncommitted files included, or from its ref when none does; remote-tracking refs are not read. The trunk is the branch origin's HEAD names, else `main`, else `master`; without one, every local branch is read. A claim belongs to a branch, so on a detached HEAD `claim` is refused. Several branches may claim one item: `claim` says who else holds it rather than refusing. There are no locks: a claim says who works on what and never excludes anyone. What one session at a time must touch — the trunk, the published site, the releases — is touched by one writer, the coordinator; workers only prepare on their own branches, and the owner decides what lands and when, when it matters. Work happens by one scheme, checked: the worktree `<worktrees>/<what>` stands on the branch `<who>/<what>` and carries a claim; `open` makes all three in one step. A claim marked `--preparing` is told when the trunk moves under it, and which commits were made on the trunk directly; `prune --branch` deletes a branch only when the trunk or an `archive/<branch>` tag holds its commits. A claim is stale when its branch is gone, or merged into the trunk that carries its file, or every item it claims is done or closed: `claims` lists it apart, `stale-claims` notes it, and `prune --write` releases it; a claim that still names a closed item among open ones is noted by `claims-on-closed-items`. Work left behind is listed by `stale` and in the summary: every branch, worktree and claim whose claim is stale, or with no sign of life (commit, step, session note, file not committed) for `staleAfter` hours, with its facts — last commit, files not committed, commits ahead of the trunk, whether it is up to date with it, items held and their status — and the next step: resume, land, archive or drop. Landings are semi-linear: a branch the trunk is an ancestor of enters it as one marker commit, a merge whose tree is the branch tip's and whose message names the items it closes in `Closes:` trailers; `land` makes it from the main checkout, the shortcut for `git merge --no-ff`, and moves the trunk only from the commit it read. From the first marker on the trunk's first-parent line every first-parent commit is a marker, or `landings-are-markers` notes it, one note per commit, which `naima waive landings-are-markers <commit>` accepts with a reason; before it nothing is asked, so a history of fast-forwards keeps working. The trunk guard holds the same line before anything lands: a git `reference-transaction` hook (git 2.28 or later), written by `naima init` and by `naima update` into the data directory's `hooks/` and named by core.hooksPath, refuses a commit, merge or fast-forward of the trunk made by hand, in one line that says to open an item and land it. It lets through what the check accepts (a marker, the record land makes after it, a commit that only adds to the tracker data or only closes items, naima init's commit), a commit that only switches the guard, a tip origin's branch of the trunk already holds (a pull), a rewind, and a commit with a `Trunk-reason:` trailer, the owner's way through, which the check then notes with its reason. Other refs cost the shell script alone; for the trunk it starts `naima guard-check`. While the guard is on the check asks from the commit that added the hook to the trunk, so a project is not noted for its past; the plugin ships the rule that every change goes through an item and lands, acknowledged as "Landing mode on". `naima guard off` turns it off for the project (the option `trunkGuard`, the hook removed), `naima guard on` back on, and `naima hello` says when it is off. A commit made on the trunk that only adds to the tracker data is accepted without a note: new files in the data directory outside `rules/`, `waivers/` and `naima.json`, lines added to an item's README.md with its meta.json untouched, and any change to a claim in `claims/` (added, rewritten by `claim --step` or removed by `release` and `prune --write`), so the coordinator files an item, appends a note, writes a diary entry or a session note, and keeps the claims without a branch; a status, a rule, a waiver, the lock or a release record still lands, from the worktree of an item of its own. naima init's commit, the one that adds `naima.json`, and the close after a landing are accepted too. A repository of the project with `changes/config.json` — the project itself, or a product it holds as a submodule — names there the paths whose change is a change of behaviour; a branch that changes one adds a change note, `changes/<date>-<slug>.md`, in the same repository. `land` refuses a branch that does not, unless `--no-change-note` gives the reason, which the marker records as a `No-change-note:` trailer; `change-notes` notes it on the branch beforehand, and is a problem for a file of `changes/` that is not a change note. `changes` prints the release notes the change notes of a range make. `naima view timeline` derives every event, with nothing stored: a gate opened is its first item reported (`created`), a gate passed its last item resolved (`closedOn`, else `fixedOn`) once none is open; an epic the same, from the items it groups; a release is a version tag, dated by its commit; a session is its note. What has no date is counted at the foot, never placed at a guess. Only what nothing derives — a decision taken elsewhere, a build handed out, a policy, an outside fact — is a record, one file per event, `events/<date>-<uuid>.md`, written by `naima event`. `naima diary` tells the records of kind `diary`, every decision with its reason, every artifact delivered (on its `deliveredOn`, when an `artifacts` type is loaded) and every session note, day by day. The plugin ships the rule that agents keep the diary on their own, one entry per decision taken with the owner or notable turn and never a log of routine work, acknowledged as "Diary mode on"; the check `diary-entries` notes, never failing, a day with more diary entries than the option `diaryPerDay` allows, and an entry that only restates a session note of its day or a decision taken that day. `pass --ack "<line>"` writes the acknowledgement line whichever plugin declares a rule's `ack` field asks an agent to give back — refused if a phrase is missing from it — and records it in the note's front matter; a note dated after 2026-10-02 missing it, or whose body no longer starts with it, is a problem (`session-note-ack`), tolerating one written before — on the day it shipped, or earlier, grandfathered like a closed item on the day `commits` shipped — since what it recorded is what the rules asked then. A note is never edited after the fact: one written without the line is accepted with a recorded waiver, `naima waive session-note-ack passes/<file> --reason "<why>" --as <who>`.

Options, each with the default it takes when nothing sets it:

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `who` |  | who works, when `naima open` is given no `--as`: the branch's first segment |
| `worktrees` | `../<main worktree's folder>-worktrees` | the directory every worktree is a folder of, relative to the main worktree |
| `exempt` | `[]` | branches the naming scheme does not apply to: names, or patterns with * |
| `maxWorkers` | `3` | how many worker worktrees (folders of the worktrees directory, on a branch the scheme applies to) may be open at once: naima open refuses another, naming the open ones, and naima hello states it in one line, saying the owner can ask to change it; a positive whole number |
| `trunkGuard` | `true` | false turns the trunk guard off: the git hook that refuses a commit, merge or fast-forward of the trunk made by hand is removed and not put back by naima update, the landing rule is not shipped, and landings-are-markers asks only from the first marker; written by naima guard off and naima guard on |
| `diaryPerDay` | `5` | how many diary entries a day may hold before the check diary-entries notes it: a positive whole number |
| `silentAfter` | `15` | minutes without a sign of life (a step posted with naima claim --step, or a commit on the branch) after which naima claims and naima summary flag a claim with a step as possibly stuck: a positive whole number |
| `staleAfter` | `24` | hours without a sign of life (a commit, a step, a session note, a file changed and not committed) after which naima stale and naima summary list a branch as stale work: a positive whole number |

**Extension points** it declares: `landing-reports`.

### naima open

Start a piece of work: a worktree <worktrees>/<what> on a new branch <who>/<what> from the trunk, and its claim on the items, in one step.

**Enforces**: Work happens on its own branch and worktree from the trunk, and its claim on the items is recorded in the same step; a branch that already exists is never reused, and the refusal says whether it is merged into the trunk; no worker worktree is opened beyond the option maxWorkers, and the refusal names the open ones and how to raise the bound.

```sh
naima open <item>... [--as <who>] [--name <what>] [--note "why"]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--as` |  | who works: the branch's first segment |
| `--name` | `the first item's slug` | what the work is: the branch's last segment and the worktree's folder |
| `--note` |  | why the branch holds the items, written in the claim |

Examples:

```sh
naima open export-drops --as agent --note "alpha channel in the exporter"
naima open export-drops export-keeps --as agent --name export-alpha
```

### naima claim

Record that this branch is working on items (writes one file on this branch).

**Enforces**: A claim belongs to a branch, never to a detached HEAD nor to the trunk, and is one file on that branch; it never locks anything: several branches may claim one item.

```sh
naima claim <item>... [--note "why"] [--step "what I am doing now"] [--preparing
naima --not-preparing]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--note` |  | why this branch holds the items; replaces the previous note |
| `--step` |  | what the branch's worker is doing now, recorded with the instant it was posted and replacing the previous step; naima claims and naima summary show it, and how long ago it was posted; items are optional once the branch holds a claim |
| `--preparing` |  | mark the branch as being prepared to enter the trunk: from then on naima check notes every commit the trunk takes that the branch lacks, and every one committed on the trunk directly; items are optional |
| `--not-preparing` |  | drop the mark |

Examples:

```sh
naima claim export-drops export-keeps --note "alpha channel in the exporter"
naima claim --preparing
naima claim --step "running the gates"
```

### naima release

Drop this branch's claim on items; the last one removes the file, unless the branch is being prepared (claim --preparing).

**Enforces**: Only this branch's own claim is dropped, and only on items it holds; while the branch is being prepared, the emptied file is kept.

```sh
naima release <item>...
```

Examples:

```sh
naima release export-drops
```

### naima claims

Who holds what, recombined from every branch, with what each branch's worker is doing now.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it only reads; a claim whose last sign of life (its step, or its branch's last commit) is more than silentAfter minutes old (15 here) is flagged possibly stuck; a stale claim (branch gone or merged into the trunk, or every item closed) is listed apart, at the end, and released by naima prune --write.

```sh
naima claims [--branch <b>] [--json]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--branch` |  | only the claim of this branch |
| `--json` |  | print the claims as JSON: each branch's items, note, step, minutes since its last sign of life and marks, the items more than one branch holds, and the silentAfter threshold |

Examples:

```sh
naima claims
naima claims --branch fix/export-alpha
naima claims --json
```

### naima land

Land a branch on the trunk as one marker commit: a merge whose tree is the branch tip's and whose message names the items it closes (Closes: trailers); the shortcut for git merge --no-ff once the trunk is the branch's ancestor.

**Enforces**: Runs from the main checkout on the trunk, clean in tracked files; refuses a branch the trunk is not an ancestor of, one still holding a claim, one that names no item (unless --tracker-only gives the reason and the branch changes only tracker data, or --meets names a requirement it meets) or an item open and not fixed; refuses --meets for an item that is not a requirement, one with no item that verifies it and passed on the branch tip, one whose proofs all passed on the trunk already, and one an item refutes, and one that changes a behaviour path of a repository with changes/config.json (the project, or a submodule) with no change note added, unless --no-change-note gives the reason; refuses, touching nothing, a branch a landing check finds failing, whatever flag is given, and one that changes what has proofs not current — a property or a test suite reading a file it changed, outside models in development — as the landing checks find them on the branch tip's files, unless --stale-proofs gives the reason; moves the trunk only from the commit it read (compare-and-swap); once landed, adds the marker to the commits of each item it closes whose type has that field, in one commit on the trunk right after the marker, so that naima close finds a commit reachable from the trunk; then prints what every landing report says of the files the landing changed, never undoing it.

```sh
naima land <branch> [--closes <item>]... [--no-change-note "<reason>"] [--stale-proofs "<reason>"] [--tracker-only "<reason>"] [--meets <requirement>]...
naima land <branch> --repair
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--repair` |  | with the tracker in a repository of its own: finish a landing that moved one repository and not the other — make the code marker the tracker's marker names, and record it in the items it closes; does nothing to a landing already paired |
| `--closes` |  | an item the landing closes, instead of those the branch claimed in its commits; repeat for several |
| `--no-change-note` |  | why the branch changes behaviour paths with no change note — a refactor, a test, nothing a person or an agent sees; recorded in the marker as a No-change-note: trailer |
| `--stale-proofs` |  | why the branch lands although proofs of what it changed are not current — a suite that runs for days, due as a long run the owner starts; recorded in the marker as a Stale-proofs: trailer |
| `--tracker-only` |  | why a branch that changes only tracker data lands — notes and decisions of a review, items filed or revised; it may close no item, and is refused when it changes any file outside the tracker data; recorded in the marker as a Tracker-only: trailer |
| `--meets` |  | a requirement the branch's work meets: met by an item that verifies it and was marked passed on the branch, never closed, so the landing may close no item; refused unless such a test passed on the branch tip, and did not already on the trunk; recorded in the marker as a Meets: trailer; repeat for several |

Examples:

```sh
naima land agent/export-alpha
naima land agent/export-alpha --closes export-drops
naima land agent/tidy-loader --no-change-note "a refactor of the loader: nothing a person or an agent sees changes"
naima land agent/scheduler --stale-proofs "the liveness property runs for two days: it is due as a long run, and the owner will start it"
naima land agent/review-notes --tracker-only "the notes and decisions of the review of the last two days"
naima land agent/export-speed --meets export-under-a-second
```

### naima guard

The trunk guard: whether it is on and runs in this clone; off turns it off for the project (recorded in naima.json, the hook removed), on turns it back on; server, on the owner's word, makes a GitHub ruleset that lets only the repository's admins push the trunk (with gh, else it says the request and the web page; --print only says them).

**Enforces**: While on, the git hook refuses a commit, merge or fast-forward of the trunk made by hand (naima guard-check says what passes); off is the owner's choice, recorded, and update does not put the hook back.

```sh
naima guard [status]
naima guard on
naima guard off
naima guard server [--print]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--print` |  | with server: say the ruleset, the gh and curl requests and the web page, and send nothing to GitHub |

Examples:

```sh
naima guard
naima guard off
naima guard on
naima guard server
naima guard server --print
```

### naima guard-check

What the trunk guard's git hook runs when the trunk is about to move: exit 0 when it may, else one line saying why not and what to do.

**Enforces**: A commit, merge or fast-forward of the trunk made by hand is refused unless every commit it adds to the first-parent line is a landing marker, the record land makes, a commit that only adds to the tracker data (a claim may also be rewritten or removed) or only closes items, naima init's commit, one that only switches the guard, or one with a Trunk-reason: trailer; a tip the upstream holds, a rewind, a ref created or deleted pass.

```sh
naima guard-check [--tracker] <old> <new>
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--tracker` |  | the move is of the tracker's trunk, in sibling mode: it takes the commits Naima makes there and landing markers |

Examples:

```sh
naima guard-check 0123abc 4567def
naima guard-check --tracker 0123abc 4567def
```

### naima changes

Print the release notes a range of commits makes, assembled from the change notes it adds to changes/, as Markdown: breaking changes first, then those that need an action, then features, behaviour changes and fixes, each with its text and what to do, and a Credits section last, as naima credits --markdown prints it; from the newest version tag (v…) to HEAD unless --from and --to say otherwise, in every repository of the project with a changes/config.json (the project itself, a submodule) unless --repo names one.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it only prints; a change note that does not parse is named on stderr.

```sh
naima changes [--from <commit>] [--to <commit>] [--repo <path>]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--from` | `the newest version tag before --to, else the first commit` | where the range starts, a commit or tag |
| `--to` | `HEAD` | where the range ends |
| `--repo` |  | the repository to read, relative to the project's root: one with a changes/config.json |

Examples:

```sh
naima changes
naima changes --from v1.0.0
naima changes --repo naima --from v1.0.0 --to main
```

### naima prune

List (or with --write remove) stale claim files: their branch is gone, or is the trunk, or merged into the trunk that carries the file, or every item they claim is closed; one only another ref carries is listed with that ref, to be dropped there. With --branch, delete a branch and its worktree, refusing one with unmerged commits that no archive/<branch> tag holds.

**Enforces**: The trunk is never pruned, and a branch with unmerged commits that no archive/<branch> tag holds is refused, and so is a worktree with anything uncommitted, inside its submodules too; a clean one is removed even when it holds a submodule; nothing is removed without --write.

```sh
naima prune [--write]
naima prune --branch <b> [--archive] [--write]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--write` |  | remove the stale claim files, or the branch and its worktree, instead of listing what would go |
| `--branch` |  | the branch to delete, with the worktree standing on it |
| `--archive` |  | tag the branch's commits as archive/<branch> before deleting it, so none is lost |

Examples:

```sh
naima prune
naima prune --write
naima prune --branch agent/old-idea --archive --write
```

### naima stale

The work left behind: every branch, worktree and claim with no sign of life for staleAfter hours, or whose branch is gone or merged, with what it holds and the next step.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it only reads; a branch counts as stale when its claim is stale (branch gone or merged into the trunk, or every item closed) or nothing happened on it for staleAfter hours (24 here) — no commit, step, session note or file changed; the next step is resume when anything is not committed, land when it is ahead of the trunk, up to date with it and holds open items, resume when it is behind, archive when no open item is claimed, drop when the trunk has all of it or the branch is gone.

```sh
naima stale [--json]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | print the stale work as JSON: each entry's facts, why it is stale, the next step and what to run |

Examples:

```sh
naima stale
naima stale --json
```

### naima pass

Write this session's note (one new file), or list the newest.

**Enforces**: A session note is one new file: earlier ones are never rewritten; a note is refused without --ack when the project's active rules ask for an acknowledgement, and --ack is refused unless it carries every phrase they ask for.

```sh
naima pass "<what changed, what is proven, what is left>" [--ack "<line>"]
naima pass --file <f> [--ack "<line>"]
naima pass --list [n] [--json]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--file` |  | read the note from a file instead of the arguments; - reads standard input |
| `--ack` |  | the acknowledgement line the project's rules ask for (naima rules --audience agents, last line) — written first, and refused if a phrase is missing from it |
| `--list` | `5` | print the newest n notes across every branch instead of writing one |
| `--json` |  | with --list, print the notes as JSON: each one's date, instant, branch, ack, file and text |

Examples:

```sh
naima pass "Exporter keeps alpha; proof owed: tests/export-keeps-alpha" --ack "Acknowledge: Quiet mode on"
naima pass --file note.md
naima pass --list 3
naima pass --list 3 --json
```

### naima event

Record an event the timeline cannot derive — a decision taken elsewhere, a build handed out, a policy, an outside fact — as one new file; everything else on `naima view timeline` is derived.

**Enforces**: An event has a YYYY-MM-DD date and a one-word kind, and is one new file; what the timeline derives is never recorded.

```sh
naima event <YYYY-MM-DD> "<what happened>" [--kind <kind>] [--at <HH:MM
naima ISO timestamp>]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--kind` | `fact` | what sort of event: decision, build, policy, fact, diary, or any word |
| `--at` | `now, for an event of today; none for an earlier day` | the moment it happened: a local time on that day (HH:MM or HH:MM:SS), or a timestamp of that day; recorded so the events of one day keep their order |

Examples:

```sh
naima event 2026-09-14 "Build 3 handed to the testers" --kind build
naima event 2026-09-20 "The vendor ended support for v1"
naima event 2026-10-05 "Work on the new engine starts from its requirements" --kind diary --at 09:30
```

### naima diary

The project's story, day by day and in order: events recorded with --kind diary, every decision with its reason, every artifact delivered, every session note; nothing stored but those files.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it reads the records, the decisions, the artifacts and the session notes, and writes nothing.

```sh
naima diary [--from <YYYY-MM-DD>] [--to <YYYY-MM-DD>] [--json]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--from` |  | the first day to tell |
| `--to` |  | the last day to tell |
| `--json` |  | print the entries as data |

Examples:

```sh
naima diary
naima diary --from 2026-10-05
naima event 2026-10-05 "The plan was entered" --kind diary
```

**Checks**, run by `naima check`

| Check | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `claims-resolve` | a claim written in this worktree names items that exist |
| `stale-claims` | a claim whose branch is gone, or is the trunk, or merged into the trunk (which then carries its file), or whose items are all closed, no longer stands for work in progress: one note per stale claim, naming the command that releases it |
| `claims-on-closed-items` | a claim that still names an item already closed, while the claim stands for other open work, is a note naming the command that releases the item; a claim whose items are all closed is stale-claims' note, and a closed item the branch you stand on claims is closed-not-claimed's problem |
| `worktree-policy` | every worktree but the main one is <worktrees>/<what> on the branch <who>/<what>, every local branch but the trunk is <who>/<what>, and every worktree carries a claim — one with commits the trunk lacks and no claim, now or released in those commits, nor a session note, is a problem for the worktree being checked, and (unless naima check --all-worktrees) a note naming any other worktree in the same state; a worktree outside <worktrees> that nothing holds is not Naima's (made before it, or by plain git) and is only a note |
| `trunk-moved-while-preparing` | a branch whose claim is marked preparing is told every commit the trunk took that it lacks, and which of them the trunk's reflog records as committed on the trunk directly |
| `closed-not-claimed` | no archived item (one in a type that is not creatable, where naima close moves it) is claimed by the branch you stand on: what no-closing-own-claims refuses on a write, asserted on the tracker as it is, hand edits included; on the trunk nothing is asked, since a claim naming the trunk is stale |
| `session-note-ack` | a session note dated after 2026-10-02 carries the acknowledgement line it was written with (naima pass --ack), and its body still begins with it — a rule change afterwards never invalidates a note already written, since what was asked of it then is what it recorded |
| `landings-are-markers` | from the first landing marker on the trunk's first-parent line (a merge whose first parent the second contains, whose tree is the second's, with a Closes:, a Tracker-only: or a Meets: trailer), every first-parent commit is a marker: a fast-forward, a commit made on the trunk, a merge not up to date, or one without a Closes: naming an item done or fixed — or a Tracker-only: trailer giving why a merge that changes only tracker data lands, or a Meets: trailer naming the requirement a merge meets, closing nothing if need be — is a note naming it, one note per commit, with the commit as its subject so that a waiver can accept it. A commit made on the trunk that only adds to the tracker data — new files in the data directory outside rules/, waivers/ and naima.json, and lines added to an item's README.md, its meta.json untouched — is accepted without a note, and so is a commit that only closes items as naima close does (each moved whole from its type's folder to the closed archive), the commit right after a marker that only adds the marker to the commits of items it closes, the record naima land makes, and naima init's commit, the one that adds naima.json. Any other tracker step that changes more than it adds (an update of Naima, a waiver, a release record, an epic set done) is made on an item's branch and landed. Before the first marker nothing is asked, unless the trunk guard is on: then the check asks from the commit that added the guard's hook to the trunk, so a project is not noted for what it committed before the guard; a commit the owner let through the guard with a Trunk-reason: trailer is a note that gives the reason. In sibling mode, where Naima commits every write to the tracker itself with a Naima-Command: trailer naming the command, such a commit is accepted, and from the first of them on, a commit of the tracker's trunk without one is a note: it was made by hand |
| `landings-paired` | with the tracker in a repository of its own, every landing is made on both sides and their trailers match: a tracker marker (Closes:, Code:) whose code commit the code's trunk does not hold, or a code marker (Tracker:) whose tracker commit is not a marker on the tracker's trunk naming the code it merged, is a problem naming naima land <branch> --repair, which finishes it; a landing whose code marker is not recorded in the commits of the items it closes is a note naming the same command |
| `branches-paired` | with the tracker in a repository of its own, the tracker stands on the branch of the code's name (its trunk on the code's trunk), so work on code branch X writes to tracker branch X — any naima command pairs them, creating the tracker's branch from its trunk; a commit of the branch, in either repository, that does not name the other repository's commit in its Tracker: or Code: trailer is a note, and so is a missing trailer hook |
| `diary-entries` | as notes, never failing: a day with more diary entries than the coordination option diaryPerDay (5 by default), and a diary entry that only restates a session note of its day or a decision taken that day, which naima diary already shows |
| `change-notes` | every file of a changes/ directory that has a changes/config.json — the project's own, or a submodule's — is a change note that parses; on a branch other than the trunk, one whose commits change a behaviour path that file names with no change note added is a note, as naima land would refuse it |
| `ready-work-waiting` | no worker slot is idle while the ready queue holds approved work no branch holds: the coordinator starts the next on its own |

**Views**, printed by `naima view <name>`

| View | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `timeline` | when each gate opened and passed, each epic began and finished, each release and session — derived from the items and git, nothing stored; undated ones counted at the foot |

**Directories** it owns under the tracker root: `claims/`, `passes/`, `events/`.

**Summary sections**: `where we were`, `in hand`, `worker limit`, `ready queue`, `stale work`, `trunk-guard`.

**Write hooks**, run on every item write

| Hook | What it does |
|---|---|
| `no-closing-own-claims` | archiving an item (a move to a type that is not creatable, as naima close does) that the branch you stand on claims is refused unless --force: a branch does not close its own items on the strength of its own tests; a claim naming the trunk is stale, never the trunk's own, and refuses nothing |

**Setup**, put in place by `naima init` and `naima update` where missing

| Step | What it puts in place |
|---|---|
| `trunk-guard` | the trunk guard, a git reference-transaction hook in the data directory's hooks, which refuses a commit, merge or fast-forward of the trunk made by hand; core.hooksPath pointed there where unset. Nothing while the option trunkGuard is false |

**UI views**, the tabs of the provisional window

| View | Title | Where | What it shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claims` | Claims | first screen | who holds what, recombined from every branch, and the items more than one branch holds; its data is `naima claims --json` |
| `timeline` | Timeline | tab | the project's events — gates, epics, releases, sessions, records — derived from the items and git, oldest first |
| `notes` | Session notes | tab | the newest session notes, across every branch, newest first; `?n=` says how many (5); its data is `naima pass --list [n] --json` |

**Shipped rules**, active in every project that loads the plugin, listed by `naima rules`

| Rule | Title | For | Strength | Enforced by | Verified by | Ack |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agents-keep-the-diary` | Agents keep the diary: one entry per decision taken with the owner or notable turn, never a log of routine work | agents | must | `diary-entries` | `diary-entries` | `Diary mode on` |
| `workers-post-their-step` | Workers post their current step; the coordinator reads them and reports a silent worker | agents | must |  | `agent` |  |
| `changes-land-through-items` | Every change goes through an item, its worktree and naima land; the trunk is never committed by hand | agents | must | `landings-are-markers` | `landings-are-markers` | `Landing mode on` |

## triage

Priority, impact, effort, confidence; the urgency ranking built from them; parked, wontfix and dropped deferrals; authoritative documents.

Its contributions' qualified ids are `triage/<name>`.

Four fields rank an item, and no more. `effort` is never derived: nothing in a report says what a fix costs, and a size guessed from the wording is how an XL hides inside an S. `triage derive` infers only `confidence`, from the page's own words — an evidence verb negated up to three words before it ("could not be reproduced") reads as `unclear`, never `measured` — and stamps `triagedBy: derived` so a value a person set is never overwritten. Urgency is the sum of every plugin's rank terms, lower first; this plugin adds impact (×1.5), priority (×1.2) and effort (×0.3), each by its value's rank; an unset impact or priority counts as the middle of its scale, an unset effort as its largest size (XL), so an item nobody has sized sinks. A parked priority, or a wontfix or dropped status, is a deferral: `reopensWhen` says what would make it worth re-arguing, `naima view parked` lists every one, and a page still left as its unfilled template is a problem. `options.documents` in naima.json (`plugins.triage.options.documents`) names which documents are authoritative and which are retired — path → { "says", "retired" }; `naima guide` prints the list, and a check notes a retired one still named from a current one. `naima view next` (and the summary it feeds) carries an age column, derived at read time from `triagedOn` or `created`, never stored; a `now` item no branch's claim names is marked unclaimed, and `unclaimed-now-item-aging` notes one open past `options.maxNowAgeDays` (default 3).

Options, each with the default it takes when nothing sets it:

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `maxNowAgeDays` | `3` | how many days a `now` item may sit unclaimed before a check notes it |

### naima triage

Coverage of the four fields; set them; list what needs a human; derive what the page proves.

**Enforces**: The four fields take only their declared values, through the write hooks; derive writes only with --write.

```sh
naima triage
naima triage set <item> field=value...
naima triage missing
naima triage derive [--write]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--write` |  | with derive: save the derived values instead of reporting them |

Examples:

```sh
naima triage
naima triage set export-drops impact=high priority=now effort=M
naima triage missing
naima triage derive --write
```

**Fields**

| Field | Kind | Applies to | Meaning | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `priority` | enum | every type | when | `now` being worked on, or the next thing anyone should pick up; `next` this cycle, once now is clear; `later` real, agreed, not scheduled; `parked` deliberately not being done; the reason is on the page |
| `impact` | enum | every type | if this stays as it is, who notices | `blocker` stops a release, or loses someone's work; `high` a newcomer would hit it and not come back; `medium` noticeable, worked around; `low` cosmetic, or only we would notice |
| `effort` | enum | every type | what it costs — never derived | `S` under an hour; `M` half a day; `L` a day or two; `XL` more, or unknown until broken up |
| `confidence` | enum | every type | do we understand the item | `measured` reproduced and measured; `diagnosed` the cause is known; `reported` as reported, not yet looked at; `unclear` nobody knows yet |
| `triagedBy` | enum | every type | set to derived when a tool inferred the fields | `derived` inferred by naima triage derive |
| `triagedOn` | date | every type | when a person last triaged the item |  |
| `reopensWhen` | string | every type | on a parked, wontfix or dropped item: what would make it worth re-arguing — prose, or a link to the item or document that would |  |

**Checks**, run by `naima check`

| Check | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `deferred-says-why` | a parked, wontfix or dropped item's page says why — not left as the template it was created with |
| `retired-document-still-linked` | no current authoritative document still names a retired one |
| `unclaimed-now-item-aging` | a `now` item open past options.maxNowAgeDays (3) with nobody's claim on it |

**Views**, printed by `naima view <name>`

| View | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `next` | open items, most urgent first |
| `parked` | every parked, wontfix or dropped item, with what would reopen it |

**Summary sections**: `next up`.

**Guide sections**, printed first by `naima guide`

| Section | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `authoritative-documents` | which documents are authoritative, and which are retired |

**Rank terms**, added to every item's urgency: `impact`, `priority` (urgent: `now`), `effort`.

**Write hooks**, run on every item write

| Hook | What it does |
|---|---|
| `triage-stamps-its-date` | a change to priority, impact, effort or confidence — by naima set, triage set, or any command — stamps triagedOn with today and drops triagedBy: derived; a write triage derive marks derived stamps nothing |

**UI views**, the tabs of the provisional window

| View | Title | Where | What it shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `next` | Next up | first screen | the open items, most urgent first, ranked as `naima view next` ranks them; `?n=` says how many (15); its data is `naima view --json next` |

## gates

Named release conditions backed by items.

Its contributions' qualified ids are `gates/<name>`.

A gate is the set of items that must be settled before something may happen — a release, a merge. An item joins a gate by carrying `gate: <name>`. Gates are configured, never hard-coded, and any plugin may contribute one through the contract; `naima gates` lists them all. `naima gate new` declares one in the project's configuration and `naima gate add` puts items on it, so nobody edits naima.json by hand. A gate with a `due` date (and, optionally, a `version`) is a milestone: `naima gates` and `naima queue` say the days left, and a check warns once it is overdue. An item whose type carries the `group` trait — an epic — stands on a gate for the items it groups. A coverage list is a normative list the project keeps elsewhere — paid features, limits, API endpoints — named by its source, a JSON file and a path in it, or files and a regular expression, and read from it on every run, never copied. A proving item names the entry it proves in `covers`; `naima coverage` prints every entry with its test or NO TEST, `--check` exits 1 on one, and a gate that lists it in `coverage` is blocked by each.

Options, each with the default it takes when nothing sets it:

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `gates` | `{}` | `plugins.gates.options.gates` in `naima-tracker/naima-data/naima.json`, written by `naima gate new`: gate name → { "title", "says", "holdsOn", "due", "version" }. due (YYYY-MM-DD) makes the gate a milestone; version is what it ships as. holdsOn "code" (the default) waits for code, not proof: a fixed item that owes only its proving gesture, and the gestures themselves, are owed but do not block. holdsOn "proof": every open item on the gate blocks it. |
| `coverage` | `{}` | `plugins.gates.options.coverage` in `naima-tracker/naima-data/naima.json`: list name → { "says", and one source: "json" (a file from the project root) with "path" (keys joined by dots, * for every element or value) and "key" (the field naming an entry when elements are objects, default id); or "files" (paths or patterns with * and **) with "pattern" (a regular expression; each match is an entry, its first group when it has one) }. A gate requires lists with "coverage": [names]. |

**Extension points** it declares: `gates`.

**Uses**, declared by other plugins: fields `fixedOn`, `runBy`, `humanBecause`; relations `verifies`, `verified-by`.

### naima gates

Every gate, whoever declared it, and whether it holds; --check exits 1 if one does not.

**Enforces**: With --check, every listed gate holds: exit 1 if one does not.

```sh
naima gates [name...] [--check] [--json]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--check` |  | exit 1 when a listed gate does not hold |
| `--json` |  | print the gates as JSON: each one's name, title, timing, whether it holds, and the items blocking it or owed |

Examples:

```sh
naima gates
naima gates first-public --check
naima gates --json
```

### naima gate

Declare a gate — a milestone, with a date and a version — put items on it or take them off, and show one; writes go to naima.json and to the items, validated, through the write hooks.

**Enforces**: Writes to naima.json and to the items are validated and pass the write hooks.

```sh
naima gate new <name> "<title>" [--says <s>] [--due YYYY-MM-DD] [--version <v>] [--holds-on code|proof] [--coverage <list>,...] [--full-suite]
naima gate set <name> [--title <t>] [--says <s>] [--due YYYY-MM-DD] [--version <v>] [--holds-on code|proof] [--coverage <list>,...] [--full-suite
naima --no-full-suite]
naima gate add <gate> <item>...
naima gate remove <gate> <item>...
naima gate show <gate>
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--title` |  | gate set: its new title |
| `--says` |  | gate new and set: what the gate is for, in one sentence |
| `--due` |  | gate new and set: the date it is due, YYYY-MM-DD, which makes it a milestone; with set, "" takes the date off |
| `--version` |  | gate new and set: the version it ships as; with set, "" takes it off |
| `--holds-on` |  | gate new and set: "code" (the default) waits for code and lets proof be owed; "proof" waits for every proof too |
| `--coverage` |  | gate new and set: the coverage lists it requires, comma-separated: each entry with NO TEST blocks it; with set, "" takes them off |
| `--full-suite` |  | gate new and set: a release gate, which holds only when every gate that is part of the full suite holds too: every property current, every test suite passing |
| `--no-full-suite` |  | gate set: no longer a release gate that waits for the full suite |

Examples:

```sh
naima gate new beta "Public beta" --says "the first outside users" --due 2026-12-01 --version 0.9
naima gate add beta bugs/export-drops-alpha epics/onboarding
naima gate remove beta bugs/export-drops-alpha
naima gate show beta
naima gate new v1 "First release" --version 1.0 --full-suite
naima gate set beta --due ""
naima gate set beta --due 2026-12-15
```

### naima queue

Open items on a gate, split by whose hands the proof needs; at its foot, the summary sections that stand beside the work, such as the metrics. With --role, one role's queue instead.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it prints derived state, never stored.

```sh
naima queue [gate] [--human] [--role <role>]
naima queue [gate] --ready
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--human` |  | also list the items that need a person or a build, with why |
| `--ready` |  | list the ready queue instead: the open items the owner approved at the close of a meeting, in the order they start — what the owner said to start now first, then by priority |
| `--role` |  | list one role's open items, most urgent first — on the gate, when one is named, else every open item: a role any loaded plugin contributes |

Examples:

```sh
naima queue
naima queue first-public --human
naima queue --role tester
naima queue first-public --role implementer
naima queue --ready
```

### naima coverage

Each normative list the project declares — read from its source now, never copied — every entry with the test that proves it, or NO TEST.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it reads each list from its source every time, never a copy, and marks an entry no test proves NO TEST.

```sh
naima coverage [list...] [--check] [--json]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--check` |  | exit 1 when an entry has NO TEST, or a list's source cannot be read |
| `--json` |  | print each list as JSON: list, says, entries (entry, tests), error |

Examples:

```sh
naima coverage
naima coverage paid --check
```

### naima ready

The open items that wait on nothing still open -- every `blocked-by` target settled -- most urgent first: what can start now; on a gate, only its items.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it prints derived state, never stored.

```sh
naima ready [gate] [--json]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | print the items as data |

Examples:

```sh
naima ready
naima ready first-public
```

### naima order

Every open item in an order that puts it after everything it waits on (`blocked-by`), with its depth -- how many waits stand before it; items stuck on a cycle are listed apart.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it prints derived state, never stored.

```sh
naima order [gate] [--json]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | print the order as data |

Examples:

```sh
naima order
naima order first-public
```

**Fields**

| Field | Kind | Applies to | Meaning | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `covers` | strings | every type | the entries of the coverage lists this proving item proves: `<entry>`, or `<list>:<entry>` to say which list; comma-separated |  |
| `gate` | enum | every type | the gates this item is what is waited for: any gate a loaded plugin contributes — the project's own, or a plugin's — one, or a list of several | the name of any contribution to `gates`; one, or a list of several |

**Checks**, run by `naima check`

| Check | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `gated-proof-is-gated` | an open item that verifies an open gated item carries a gate itself |
| `milestone-overdue` | warns when a gate with a due date is past it and does not hold |
| `coverage-lists` | a coverage list's source can be read; an item's covers names an entry its list holds |
| `dependencies-acyclic` | no open items wait on each other in a cycle of blocked-by links: none of them could ever start |
| `dependencies-wait-on-work` | every blocked-by names work: a requirement is not work, so a wait on it is a note -- wait on what delivers or proves it |

**Summary sections**: `gates`.

**Rank terms**, added to every item's urgency: `gate`.

**Migrations** of its own data, run by `naima update` after the core's; its format is 2:

- format 1 → 2: the top-level gates key of naima.json moves to plugins.gates.options.gates

**UI views**, the tabs of the provisional window

| View | Title | Where | What it shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gates` | Gates | first screen | every gate and whether it holds, with the items blocking it and those owing only proof, as `naima gates` reports them; its data is `naima gates --json` |
| `coverage` | Coverage | tab | each normative list the project declares, read from its source now, every entry with the test that proves it or NO TEST |

## epics

Epics: bodies of work that group items, their status and progress derived from them.

Its contributions' qualified ids are `epics/<name>`.

An epic groups items: `naima epic add <epic> <item>...` links each item `part-of` the epic (the inverse, `has-part`, is derived). Its status is derived, never set: open while any item it groups is open, done when every one is closed. `naima epic` shows each open epic with its progress — n of m closed — what it waits for, and whose hands. An epic can carry a gate (`naima gate add <gate> <epic>`): its type carries the `group` trait, so the gate stands for the items it groups.

**Uses**, declared by other plugins: fields `runBy`, `gate`; relations `verified-by`.

### naima epic

Each epic with its progress — n of m closed, what it waits for and whose hands — or put items in an epic and take them out.

**Enforces**: Only an epic groups items and never itself, and its status follows its items: setting it against them is refused.

```sh
naima epic [<epic>...] [--all] [--json]
naima epic add <epic> <item>...
naima epic remove <epic> <item>...
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` |  | list the done epics too |
| `--json` |  | print each epic's progress as JSON: epic, title, status, closed, total, open, gates, hands |

Examples:

```sh
naima epic
naima epic onboarding --json
naima epic add onboarding bugs/export-drops-alpha todos/first-run-copy
naima epic remove onboarding todos/first-run-copy
```

### type: epics

Epics: a body of work that groups items: its status follows them, and a gate on it stands for them. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/epics/`; a new one starts as `open`.

Traits: `group`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | open |  | some item it groups is still open, or it groups none yet |
| `done` | done |  | every item it groups is closed |

**Link relations** — only the direction written is stored; the inverse is derived when read.

| Relation | Inverse | Reads as |
|---|---|---|
| `part-of` | `has-part` | is part of |
| `has-part` | `part-of` | groups |

**Checks**, run by `naima check`

| Check | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `epics` | an item is part of an epic, never of an item of another type; an open epic groups at least one item; an epic's status is the one its items give it, as the epic-status hook writes it, hand edits included |

**Summary sections**: `epics`.

**Write hooks**, run on every item write

| Hook | What it does |
|---|---|
| `epic-status` | an epic's status follows its items: set on every write of the epic, and of an item it groups; setting it against them is refused |

## discussions

Discussions: questions that need time with a person, gathered on the agenda of meetings.

Its contributions' qualified ids are `discussions/<name>`.

A discussion is an item of its own (`naima new discussions "<topic>"`): the question, the options, and, once decided, the decision, recorded with `naima decide <discussion> "<decision>"`. It links the items it is about with `concerns`. A meeting is a gate whose agenda is the discussions on it: it names who it needs, takes place whenever they are present unless it has a date, and holds once every discussion on it is decided. Like any item a discussion takes a priority, a gate or milestone, and an optional date (`due`): `naima meeting <m>` orders the agenda, what is due or has priority now first, then what blocks a release or a milestone (soonest first), then the rest; a later or parked priority, or a date to come, defers it, and it stays queued, last. `naima meeting new` declares one, `naima meeting add` puts discussions on its agenda, `naima meeting` shows the agendas, and `naima hello` names each meeting with discussions to take so the agent opens with its agenda. Deciding writes only fields Naima fills and the status `decided`, flagged `filled`, so the trunk guard takes it on the trunk; it files follow-up work only with the owner's yes (`--follow-up` with `--consent`), linked from the new item. `naima meeting <m> --close` ends a meeting: it groups the decisions not yet turned into work into packages, one per open item they concern, and proposes them; with `--consent`, the owner's yes restated, it records the choice on each item as a `ready` record, queued by default or to start now (`--start`), nothing for a package `--skip` names, and marks each decision `packaged`. `naima queue --ready` lists the ready queue, and the coordinator starts the next item on it whenever a worker slot is free.

Options, each with the default it takes when nothing sets it:

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `meetings` | `{}` | `plugins.discussions.options.meetings` in `naima-tracker/naima-data/naima.json`, written by `naima meeting new`: meeting name → { "title", "needs" (who must be present; the owner by default), "on" (a date, YYYY-MM-DD; without one, whenever they are present) }. Each meeting is a gate of that name. |

**Uses**, declared by other plugins: fields `gate`, `due`.

### naima meeting

Declare a meeting — who it needs, and a date or whenever they are present — put discussions on its agenda, and show the agenda.

**Enforces**: Only a discussion goes on a meeting's agenda, and a meeting is written to naima.json validated, as the next load reads it.

```sh
naima meeting [<name>]
naima meeting <name> --close [--consent "<the owner's yes>"] [--start <item>,...] [--skip <item>,...]
naima meeting new <name> "<title>" [--needs <who>,...] [--on YYYY-MM-DD]
naima meeting add <meeting> <discussion>...
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--close` |  | end the meeting: group the decisions not yet turned into work into packages, one per open item they concern, and propose them; with --consent, record each package's choice on its item: queued (the default) or to start now |
| `--consent` |  | --close: the owner's yes to the packages, restated: recorded on each item's ready record |
| `--start` |  | --close: the packages (their items) the owner said to start now; comma-separated or repeated |
| `--skip` |  | --close: the packages the owner said not to queue now; comma-separated or repeated |
| `--needs` |  | meeting new: who must be present, comma-separated; the owner when not given |
| `--on` |  | meeting new: a fixed date, YYYY-MM-DD; without one, it takes place whenever the people it needs are present |

Examples:

```sh
naima meeting
naima meeting new owner "With the owner"
naima meeting new review "Design review" --needs owner,reviewer --on 2026-11-03
naima meeting add owner discussions/plugin-names
naima meeting owner
naima meeting owner --close
naima meeting owner --close --consent "yes, queue them; start the export fix now" --start bugs/export-alpha
```

### naima decide

Record the decision a discussion reached and mark it decided — a commit the trunk takes, during a meeting; a follow-up is filed only with the owner's yes.

**Enforces**: A discussion is decided only with its decision recorded; follow-up work is filed only with --consent, the owner's yes restated, and linked from the discussion.

```sh
naima decide <discussion> "<decision>" [--follow-up "<title>" --consent "<the owner's yes, restated>"]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--follow-up` |  | the title of a todos item to file for the work the decision calls for; needs --consent |
| `--consent` |  | the owner's yes to filing the follow-up, restated: recorded on its page |

Examples:

```sh
naima decide discussions/plugin-names "Call them playbooks"
naima decide discussions/meeting-time "Whenever the owner is present" --follow-up "Say the agenda at session start" --consent "yes, file it"
```

### type: discussions

Discussions: a question that needs time with a person, not a quick answer: the topic, the question, the options, and the decision once taken; on a meeting's agenda. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/discussions/`; a new one starts as `open`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | open |  | not decided yet: it waits for a meeting with the people it needs |
| `decided` | done | filled | decided: the decision is recorded in its decision field |

**Fields**

| Field | Kind | Applies to | Meaning | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decision` | string | discussions | what the discussion decided, recorded by naima decide |  |
| `decisionOn` | date | discussions | when the discussion was decided, stamped by naima decide |  |
| `packaged` | date | discussions | when the decision was turned into work, stamped by naima meeting <m> --close |  |

**Link relations** — only the direction written is stored; the inverse is derived when read.

| Relation | Inverse | Reads as |
|---|---|---|
| `concerns` | `concerned-by` | is a discussion about |
| `concerned-by` | `concerns` | is discussed in |

**Checks**, run by `naima check`

| Check | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `discussions` | a decided discussion records its decision; an open one is on a meeting's agenda, or it waits for no one; a decision taken in a meeting is turned into work when the meeting closes |

**Summary sections**: `meetings`.

**Extensions** of other plugins' types and fields

- field `due`: applies to discussions

**Write hooks**, run on every item write

| Hook | What it does |
|---|---|
| `discussion-decided` | a discussion is decided only with its decision recorded |

## planning

Requirements proven by tests, specifications versioned name-vN, the owner's decisions recorded once, and the artifacts the project makes and keeps.

Its contributions' qualified ids are `planning/<name>`.

Planning as items, so each is proven or checked rather than implied by a test. A **requirement** says what must hold: the features, tests or epics that deliver it are linked `satisfies`, the tests or properties that prove it `verifies`; it is `met` only once a proof has passed and none refutes it, and `naima view requirements` traces each one. A requirement whose origin says someone other than the owner asked for it (`naima new requirements "<what>"` without `--asked-by owner`) starts `proposed`: no gate counts it as a goal, `requirements-proven` notes it, and it becomes `stated` only when the owner confirms it, `naima confirm <requirement> --words "<the owner's yes, restated>"`, which records the words in its field `confirmed`. A **specification** says how something must behave, versioned `name-vN`: `naima spec revise <spec>` opens the next version as a draft that `supersedes` the old one, one version per name is `current`, and an item that follows a spec is linked `specified-by` — work starts from the spec, and closes when the code matches it. A **decision** is a choice or a standing permission of the owner's, dated and restated in the owner's words: it `settles` the items that waited on it and `supersedes` the decision it replaces. Before asking the owner anything, an agent runs `naima decisions <words>`; after the owner answers, it records the answer with `naima new decisions`, so a settled question is never asked again. A **release** opens at its first stage (`naima new releases "<name>"`); each stage's output is recorded with `naima note`, headed `Stage: <name>` (or `Stage: <name> — skipped, decided by <who>`), and the hook refuses `status=released` while a stage is unrecorded — `naima view releases` shows what each one still owes. A **session** is a dated, append-only record of one test sitting, linked `records` to the test or tests it was for; several share a `run` name when they were sat together. It is optional — most of the time the test's own page and status say enough — and is never edited once written: a later sitting is a new session. An **artifact** is something the project makes and keeps — an analysis, a profile, a report, a dataset, a figure: `due` by a day, made by the todo or feature linked `produces`, made of `files` (paths from the project root) or its attachments, made from `inputs` (files or directories) and the data of the tests, properties or other artifacts it `uses`, and replaced by a later version that `supersedes` it. `naima set <artifact> status=delivered` refuses while a file it names is missing or it has none, and otherwise records `madeFrom` — the commit, one digest over its inputs and the data of what it uses, the moment — and `deliveredOn`, from which `naima diary` tells the delivery; neither is set by hand. `artifacts-current` notes an artifact past its due day and not delivered, a delivered one whose inputs changed since it was made, and a planned one nothing produces. The plugin ships two rules, listed by `naima rules` when the rules plugin is loaded: requirements are elicited at every prompt of the owner, each with how it is checked or measured (a test, a property, or a metric with a budget), acknowledged as "Elicitation mode on" and held in part by `requirements-proven`, which notes a requirement nothing proves; and behaviour with states or concurrency is designed from a model first (a state machine, mCRL2, or a state machine encoded in mCRL2), its properties as items, kept in step with the code, acknowledged as "Model first mode on". Whether a change has states or concurrency is recorded at triage, in its field `stateful` (true or false), and never guessed from the code; `model-first` notes a change triaged `stateful: true` that landed with no `models` or `properties` item linked to it and no waiver of the model-first check gives the exception with its reason. It is a note, not a problem: the rule binds where the behaviour has states, and the waiver is the exception, filed. How strictly the project applies model first is its own choice, the option `modelFirst`, shown and set with `naima model-first`: `strict` (the default) keeps the rule a must and notes every such change; `advisory` makes it a should, where a new protocol or concurrency (`statefulKind: protocol`) is still noted as a must, other new behaviour is noted as advice, and a change to existing code is not noted: one triaged `statefulKind: existing`, or, untriaged, one whose files all existed at the commit the setting was adopted at (`modelFirstSince`) and none had half its lines removed; `deferred` adopts model checking later, by the gate or the date in `modelFirstUntil`: `naima model-first deferred --until <gate|date>` files at once the todo that plans it, on that gate, `model-first` notes the deferral instead of each change, and `naima hello` says it until the owner chooses. `naima init` proposes the setting to a project that has none: strict for a new project, advisory when the repository already holds substantial code (20 source files or 2000 lines), and says the question to put to the owner.

Options, each with the default it takes when nothing sets it:

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `modelFirst` | `strict` | how strictly the project applies model first: strict (a must), advisory (a should; existing code exempt unless rewritten; a new protocol or concurrency kept a must) or deferred (adopted later, by modelFirstUntil); set with naima model-first |
| `modelFirstSince` |  | the full hash of the commit the setting was adopted at: what existed there is existing code, for advisory |
| `modelFirstUntil` |  | with deferred: the gate the adoption todo stands on, or the date YYYY-MM-DD by which the owner decides |

**Uses**, declared by other plugins: fields `runBy`, `humanBecause`, `fixedOn`, `origin`; relations `verified-by`.

### naima spec

Each specification: its current version, its drafts, and the open items that follow it; or revise one into its next version.

**Enforces**: A revision is a new spec item, its next version, that supersedes the old one; the old version is kept as it was.

```sh
naima spec [--json]
naima spec revise <spec>
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | print each specification as JSON: spec, current, versions, drafts, followedBy |

Examples:

```sh
naima spec
naima spec --json
naima spec revise specs/export-format
```

### naima decisions

Search the owner's decisions before asking: the settled ones whose title or page hold every word given, newest first.

**Enforces**: Nothing: it only searches, so a settled question is looked up before it is asked again.

```sh
naima decisions [<word>...] [--all] [--json]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` |  | search the superseded and reopened decisions too |
| `--json` |  | print the decisions as JSON: item, title, status, decidedOn, standing, settles, text |

Examples:

```sh
naima decisions
naima decisions journal
naima decisions licence --all --json
```

### naima confirm

Record the owner's confirmation of a proposed requirement, one someone other than the owner filed: it becomes stated, and gates count it from then on; the owner's yes, restated, is kept on the item.

**Enforces**: Only a proposed requirement is confirmed, and only with the owner's words restated: an agent runs it after the owner said yes, never on its own judgement.

```sh
naima confirm <requirement> --words "<the owner's yes, restated>" [--by <who>]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--words` |  | the owner's yes, restated in the agent's words, recorded in the field confirmed |
| `--by` | `git's user.name` | who records it |

Examples:

```sh
naima confirm export-keeps --words "Yes, the export must keep the alpha channel"
```

### naima model-first

Show or set how strictly the project applies model first (planning option modelFirst): strict, the rule a must; advisory, a should, with code that existed before the setting exempt unless rewritten and a new protocol or concurrency kept a must; deferred until a gate or a date the owner names, which files at once the todo that plans adopting model checking there.

**Enforces**: The setting is the owner's choice: an agent sets it only after the owner said which; deferring always names a gate or a date and files its todo.

```sh
naima model-first [strict
naima advisory
naima deferred --until <gate|YYYY-MM-DD>]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--until` |  | with deferred: the gate (or milestone) the adoption todo stands on, or the date by which the owner decides |

Examples:

```sh
naima model-first
naima model-first advisory
naima model-first deferred --until v1
naima model-first deferred --until 2027-03-01
```

### type: requirements

Requirements: something the result must satisfy, stated so it can be checked: delivered by the items that satisfy it, proven by the tests or properties that verify it. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/requirements/`; a new one starts as `stated`.

Traits: `standard`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proposed` | open | proposed | filed by someone other than the owner and not yet confirmed by the owner (naima confirm): no gate counts it as a goal |
| `stated` | open |  | stated, and not yet proven |
| `met` | done |  | proven: a test or property linked to it has passed, and none refutes it |
| `dropped` | done |  | no longer required; the page says why |

### type: specs

Specifications: how something must behave, versioned name-vN: a revision is a new item that supersedes the old, and one version per name is current. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/specs/`; a new one starts as `draft`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | open |  | being written or agreed; the items that follow it wait for it |
| `current` | done |  | the version in force: work follows it, and the close flow checks the code against it |
| `superseded` | done |  | replaced by a later version, kept as history |

### type: decisions

Decisions: a choice or a standing permission of the owner's, recorded once: dated, in the owner's words restated, linked to what it settles; searched before the owner is asked. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/decisions/`; a new one starts as `settled`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settled` | done |  | in force: act on it, never ask it again |
| `reopened` | open |  | the owner reopened it: the question may be asked again, and the answer is a new decision that supersedes this one |
| `superseded` | done |  | replaced by a later decision, kept as history |

### type: releases

Releases: a release in progress, staged from pre-release checks to announcing: each stage's output recorded before the next, a skipped stage naming who decided. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/releases/`; a new one starts as `staging`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `staging` | open |  | in progress: opened at its first stage, not every stage is recorded yet |
| `released` | done |  | every stage is recorded, or skipped and said by whom; published and announced |
| `rolled-back` | done |  | a stage found an issue serious enough to stop the release; the page says why |

### type: sessions

Sessions: a dated, append-only record of one test sitting: written once and never edited to change what happened — optional, not a daily habit to enforce; the test's own page is usually enough on its own. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/sessions/`; a new one starts as `recorded`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recorded` | done |  | written; a session is never reopened — a later sitting is a new session |

### type: artifacts

Artifacts: something the project makes and keeps — an analysis, a profile, a report, a dataset, a figure: due by a day, made of files, and recorded with the commit and inputs it was made from when delivered. Items live in `naima-tracker/naima-data/artifacts/`; a new one starts as `planned`.

| Status | Category | Flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `planned` | open |  | to be made: a todo or a feature linked `produces` makes it |
| `in-progress` | open |  | being made |
| `delivered` | done |  | made and kept: its files exist, and the commit and inputs it was made from are recorded in madeFrom |
| `superseded` | done |  | replaced by a later artifact that supersedes it, kept as history |

**Fields**

| Field | Kind | Applies to | Meaning | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | string | specs | the name every version of a specification shares; set from the title when the spec is opened |  |
| `version` | number | specs | the specification's version, N in name-vN; set from the title (`… v2`), else 1 |  |
| `decidedOn` | date | decisions | when the owner decided; stamped with today when the decision is recorded |  |
| `standing` | boolean | decisions | a standing permission: the action it names may be taken again, every time, without asking |  |
| `sittingRun` | string | sessions | the name shared by every session of one sitting, when several tests were sat together |  |
| `stateful` | boolean | any type tagged `fixable` | whether the behaviour this change adds or fixes has states or concurrency (a lifecycle, a protocol, a scheduler, a retry loop, two processes sharing data): recorded at triage, true or false; when true, the change starts from a model (model-first) |  |
| `statefulKind` | enum | any type tagged `fixable` | with stateful true, which kind of change it is, recorded at triage: it matters where model first is advisory, which keeps the must for a new protocol or concurrency and exempts existing code | `protocol` adds a new protocol or new concurrency: the must holds in every setting; `new` adds other new behaviour with states: a model is required when strict, advised when advisory; `existing` changes behaviour that existed before the project adopted its model-first setting, without rewriting it: exempt when advisory |
| `confirmed` | object | requirements | the owner's confirmation of a requirement filed by someone else, written by naima confirm: { words: the owner's yes, restated; by: who recorded it; on: the day } |  |
| `due` | date | artifacts | the day it is due; past it and not delivered, naima check notes it |  |
| `inputs` | strings | artifacts | the files or directories it is made from, from the project root: with the data of the items it uses, what the digest in madeFrom covers |  |
